He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it; and He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees what you do (4) His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned (5) He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He knows what is within the breasts (6) (Al-Hadid) (Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise (1) His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things (2) He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things (3) It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it; and He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees what you do (4) His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned (5) He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He knows what is within the breasts (6) (Al-Hadid) These verses sum up, in their names and attributes, everything that will come after them in Surat al-Hadid! Attributes of power: His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things Attributes of knowledge and awareness: He is the First and the Last, the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things And His knowledge of the finest details of what is on the surface and in the depths of the earth and the sky Then, once you know that, the theme of the surah takes shape and becomes clear: being mindful of Allah watching in private and in public is the cause of awe and humility (and He is with you wherever you are). And to Allah all matters are returned: to Allah are raised the decrees, the deeds and the states, and He looks into their affairs and changes them; He guides the astray, forgives the sinners, and relieves the distressed. The verses of faith in Allah and His Messenger and following the revealed Book came, and after them the verses of the conquest! To say that there is no conquest and victory without obeying Allah and His Messenger and those in authority, from scholars and rulers (And why do you not believe in Allah while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has taken your covenant, if you are believers (8) It is He who sends down upon His servant clear verses to bring you out of darkness into light; and indeed Allah is Kind and Merciful to you (9) And why do you not spend in the cause of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought; they are greater in rank than those who spent afterwards and fought. And to each Allah has promised the best, and Allah is Aware of what you do (10) Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so He will multiply it for him, and he will have a noble reward (11) (Al-Hadid) The verse made clear that whoever spends in times of calamity and hardship is firmer in his faith when the world later opens up to him, For protection from being tempted by the world comes only through spending before the conquest and after it, and how many have failed this test: they succeed in patience and fail in gratitude. Because whoever spends before the conquest and after it, the two states are equal to him; he spends with certainty that Allah will compensate him with better, and because of his certainty of victory and spoils; while the other's certainty is weaker, so he is stingy and miserly, watching the news and events until, when the conquest comes, he spends! And so spending is the test of the ṣiddīqūn (the truthful ones) Indeed, the men who give in charity and the women who give in charity and have lent Allah a goodly loan, it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward (18) And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, it is they who are the truthful ones; and the martyrs, with their Lord, will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of Hellfire (19) (Al-Hadid) He said al-muṣṣaddiqīn , not al-mutaṣaddiqīn , and in this is a subtle meaning: that the one who gives in charity is one who believes ( muṣaddiq ) that Allah will replace it for him with better and multiply it for him, and that this is what raises him to later be among the ṣiddīqūn ; because the ṣiddīq is the one who believed Allah and His Messenger and their promises, and acted accordingly. (On the Day you see the believing men and the believing women, their light running ahead of them and on their right: "Your good tidings today are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally; that is the great attainment" (12) On the Day the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." And a wall will be set up between them with a door; its inner side has mercy, and its outer side, facing it, has punishment (13) They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you tempted yourselves, and you waited and doubted, and wishful thinking deluded you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you about Allah (14) So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your patron, and wretched is the destination (15) (Al-Hadid) The exegetes say: when the believers are on the Path together with the hypocrites, both groups have light, except that the hypocrite's light goes out; because it is an outward, external light with no reality to it, since he did not realize it in this world, so it has no reality in the Hereafter; and there the believers supplicate (they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light") (At-Tahrim) So whoever Allah has not given light from the Quran and the Sunnah in this world has no light and no share in the Hereafter (And he to whom Allah has not granted light, for him there is no light (40) (An-Nur) And the one who holds most to the Quran and the Sunnah will have the greatest light on the Day of Resurrection. You tempted yourselves: like the testing of iron when it is put to the fire, separating the impure from the pure; and so it is with hearts when they are put to the light of the Quran, for ambiguous matters are presented to them, and some of them deviate and some Allah guides; all this so that Allah may know who fears Him unseen. You tempted yourselves with doubts, so you waited with desires, and you were bewildered in the darknesses and thought them many colors while their color is one and their ways are many, and wishful thinking deluded you until you were among the dead; so for your forgetting of the Hereafter, your patron is the Fire; it is their patron from this world because they took it as an ally through desires (the Fire is surrounded by desires), and by contrast it is understood that Paradise took the believer as its ally (We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request (31) (Fussilat) Because Paradise is surrounded by hardships; they fasted from desires in this world, so in return they were given what their souls desire in Paradise; a reward from your Lord, a sufficient gift. Should the believer not race against time to perfect the light, and not let the world take him and make him forget the Hereafter? (Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth, and that they not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them are defiantly disobedient (16) Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have made clear to you the signs, that you might reason (17) (Al-Hadid) (Has the time not come) as though the believer were in a state of waiting and expecting a humility to descend upon him from the sky, and putting off the ascent of his heart up the stairways of faith; so his Lord says to him, in the gentlest address and the most delightful companionship: Is not now the right time for humility, as the verse fell upon your ears, O My servant? And when that seemed hard to him and weighed on him — how can I reach a lofty station that belongs to the scholars when I have no knowledge!? (Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah) — He answered him with ease and facilitation (that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth): that his heart be softened by the Quran, for He has made clear the disease and the cure; the disease of hardness, its cure is the Quran, softening it until it is humble. And after gentleness and encouragement, He turned to warning, cautioning whoever goes back to postponing humility not to be like the People of the Book, over whom a long time passed without a Book, so their hearts hardened, And I think the People of the Book meant here are the Jews; because they are the ones whose hearts are hard (Then your hearts hardened after that, so they are like stones..) And at the end of Surat al-Hadid He spoke about the opposite state to hardness, which is the tenderness found in Christianity, and that Allah forbids resembling the People of the Book even in their states of heart, so that one has neither hardness of heart like the Jews nor the excessive tenderness that keeps them from establishing the prescribed punishments, as with the Christians -and its explanation will come in its place-. (Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death) so that you come to know that He is able to revive dead hearts through His remembrance, so do not think it unlikely that this happens, nor the guidance of the astray and the disbeliever until he becomes among the most fearful of people. (We have made clear to you the signs, that you might reason) here He has made clear to you the head of the matter: fear of Allah; and that the fruit of knowledge is awe, and that nothing in it is obscure or difficult; so is there any person of reason who will take these words? And in the verse is that Allah does not approve disbelief for His servants, and does not approve humiliation for His believing servant, nor little and weak faith; so He wanted to stir his heart to seek more faith and ascend its stairways, and not to be content with the lower rank of it (And you will be superior if you are believers) (Al Imran). And He placed around the verse of the heart's humility two verses about the world! Above it and below it, on the right page and on the left, like a flowing river engulfing it and besieging it (and wishful thinking deluded you…) on the right page, (Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement and adornment..) on the left page. (Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children — like the example of a rain whose plants please the tillers; then it dries and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion (20) Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty (21) (Al-Hadid) He turned from awe and humility, in which time is held still and slowed, to making clear the reason they do not attain such states, namely racing in the world and chasing after it; and the whole Quran describes the world briefly: play and amusement, except here in Surat al-Hadid, where He detailed it more (play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children). He is saying that the cause of hardness of heart and distance from the remembrance of Allah is preoccupation with wealth and children, and this is the trial that turns the heart away from the Quran and remembrance (And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial and that Allah has with Him a great reward (28) (Al-Anfal). So He added to their knowledge two more pieces of knowledge; as for competing in increase and scattering, this is what distracted them from remembering the Hereafter and worship (Competition in increase diverted you until you visited the graves). Then came the completion of the advice (O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, it is they who are the losers (9) (Al-Munafiqun) (O you who have believed, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may be successful (45) So if this fighter, amid war and blood and severed heads, was commanded to remember Allah, and not to let the scenes of death distract him from remembrance! And that the firmness of his foot and his victory lie in remembrance. Had Allah exempted anyone from remembrance, He would have exempted the fighter! So what of one who is busy with buying and trade? (And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much, that you may succeed (10) And when they saw a transaction or a diversion, they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers" (11) (Al-Jumu'ah) And He praised a people whom the world did not distract from His remembrance (Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah. They fear a Day in which the hearts and eyes will turn about (37) (An-Nur) And once again He makes clear to us that the cause of fearing Allah unseen and being in awe of Him is remembering Him with the heart, the tongue and deeds. There, when time stands still and movement settles: if a verse stirred your heart and spread longing, then stop! And repeat it until the tears flow and the soul ascends the stairways of humility; and the last does not happen to one who ignores a verse that stirred his heart, his concern being the end of the surah. And what harm would it do you if you fell behind in your daily portion because there is a verse that softened your heart? This is better for you than gathering gold and silver in the old crucibles. And part of the understanding of the righteous was that when their eyes wept from awe, they wiped their tears and spread them over the whole face, so that the whole face would not be touched by the Fire! (Sifat al-Safwah). A dead heart revived by humility, and a heart that was alive killed by the world (like the example of a rain whose plants please the tillers; then it dries and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris) the Quran had been its spring, then when the world came loose upon it, it made it forget the Quran and night prayer; so it reverted to its first state of hardness and heedlessness, and the calamity returned to it. (No calamity strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being. Indeed that, for Allah, is easy (22) In order that you not despair over what has eluded you and not exult over what He has given you. And Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful (23) Those who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess. And whoever turns away, then indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy (24) (Al-Hadid) And the one who reflects finds that the right page facing this verse is, on the left page, (Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death…) (In it is an indication that He, the Exalted, softens hearts after their hardness, and guides the bewildered after their straying, and relieves distress after its severity) (Ibn Kathir) Decreeing the calamity is easy for Him, and lifting it is easy for Him. And when He pointed out that the difficult is made easy, He pointed out the pitfalls of relief! Swaggering in one's walk and being deluded by the world, and it made him forget that it is a trial; and delusion and boasting lead to stinginess in spending, so they withhold wealth, and use their standing to command people to be stingy! For he has reached the most extreme state of miserliness and greed That he commands people to be stingy! And this is undoubtedly a trait of the hypocrite (they enjoin what is wrong). And among the wisdoms of adversity is expelling impurity and softening the hard heart (Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened) (Al-An'am) So whoever's heart hardens in calamity has increased the adversity upon himself, and whoever is severe, Allah is severe with him. (We have already sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for the people, and so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Almighty (25) And We have already sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and scripture; and among them is he who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient (26) Al-Hadid The one who reflects on the Quran notices that after verses commanding justice, the messengers and the scriptures are mentioned immediately; to point out that the Shariah is the best way to achieve justice in the self and in society, as in An-Nisa: (..be persistently upholders of justice…) and after it (Believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger..) and Al-An'am (And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative…) and after it (And this is My path, which is straight, so follow it..) and it is repeated in Surat al-Hadid as well. (and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain justice) He paired the Book with justice, so whoever takes hold of the Book establishes justice even against himself, and becomes just in his character, balanced in his temperament, moderate in all his affairs, his private self the same as his public self, nothing at odds between them; just! (O you who have believed, be persistently upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not desire, lest you not be just. And if you distort or refuse, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware (135) (An-Nisa) He called them by the name of faith, for nothing befits the believer but justice toward himself and his society; it does not befit him to lean with whims and turn away from the truth once it has become clear to him. (that the people may maintain justice) He omitted the object (in what do they maintain justice?) so that it is unrestricted and general, even in their dealings with tiny ants and grasses. And He revealed to a prophet: “Why not just one ant” that you burned? And in fiqh it is disliked to tread on green meadows with one's foot or one's mount without need. (And Allah is greater in might) (An-Nisa) He is severe in might in punishment and retribution, and it also includes that His might is severe in reviving hearts that have rusted; and when the Chosen One (peace be upon him) witnessed hearts changing between disbelief and faith, his most frequent oath was “No, by the Turner of hearts” because he witnessed the power after knowing it. His might is severe even in guidance and mercy. So that creation turns to Him seeking guidance from Him alone, for He is the One able to grant it and the Subjugator above His servants, and so they do not rely on their educational and psychological methods alone, even though they are means that should be taken. (and so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen) If you establish the religion, you have supported Allah and His messengers, and He qualified both with "unseen"! Because the true establishment of the religion is in the unseen, in hiding and within, where no one sees it “O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in the unseen and the seen” And the greatest victory achieved in the unseen by a believer is that he fears Allah and sheds tears in solitude far from people (Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah) And he commands himself to do right and forbids himself from wrong, then his society; not the reverse! (And We sent down iron) And when hearts thought their change unlikely, and souls found it impossible to imagine being turned from their natures, and because some souls despaired of being set right and turned away, He reminded them with a fiery example: the heart is like iron; does it not, when smelted in fire, melt and its properties change? From it are made pots and vessels after it had nearly rusted and lost its worth (And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], "O mountains, repeat praises with him, and the birds." And We made pliable for him iron (10) [Commanding him], "Make full coats of mail and calculate the links, and work righteousness. Indeed I, of what you do, am Seeing" (11) (Saba) Indeed, the One who softened iron is able, through the Quran, to soften hearts by guiding them after straying, humbling them after their roughness, uniting them after division, and setting right the heart of one who has despaired and lost hope of setting himself right. (And We made pliable) He attributed the softening of iron to Allah the Exalted and used the "We" of majesty; because iron is greatly hard, and none can soften it but its Creator; so just as He softened iron for David (peace be upon him), He is able to soften hearts and set souls right by His bounty, mercy and generosity. I had wondered why Allah did not mention David (peace be upon him) in Surat al-Hadid!? And mentioned Noah and Abraham (peace be upon them)? The answer may be that the iron here is the figurative, not the material: softening the heart, and faith and humility through constant mindfulness (and He is with you wherever you are). Striving, spiritual exercises and purification of hearts, if they are not upon the guidance of the Quran and the Sunnah, have no effect. And for this reason, after it He warned against innovations, extremism and harshness in matters of faith, as the Christians did; they had states of faith, with softness and tenderness in their hearts, except that they went to extremes and innovated, so they strayed from the straight path (And We have already sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and scripture; and among them is he who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient (26) Then We sent following their footsteps Our messengers and followed them with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism, which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them except for seeking the approval of Allah, but they did not observe it with due observance. So We gave the ones who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient (27) (Al-Hadid) So the believer does not resemble the People of the Book even in their states of heart: he is not hard-hearted like the Jews, nor a monk like the Christians, nor like them in excessive softness to the point of neglecting the prescribed punishments and not establishing justice among people. And He said in the verse of the prescribed punishment (and do not be taken by pity for them in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day (2) (An-Nur) Do not be like the Christians, for whom religion is love without fear, tolerance without limit, and tenderness that led them to make the forbidden lawful, so wrongdoing spread among them because they neglected the prescribed limits. (and monasticism, which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them except for seeking the approval of Allah, but they did not observe it with due observance) And the meaning may be: they did not observe what Allah obligated upon them, so how would they observe what they obligated upon themselves? Whoever's self is not upright upon the command of Allah and His messengers cannot make it upright by himself, for he is more incapable of that and weaker. And whoever surrenders himself to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and obeys them without adding or subtracting in following, it is a right upon Allah to guide him to what is most upright, to grant him victory over his whims, and to raise him above himself. And that the Christians, even when they innovated, did not follow! So they are neither those who followed Allah and the messengers, nor those who stayed upright upon what they innovated; so how would Allah guide the defiantly disobedient people? And that the Christians did not observe the approval of Allah in His Oneness, so they disbelieved and said that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary (and He does not approve for His servants disbelief); had they observed His approval, they would not have disbelieved. And this is a rebuttal to the innovating Sufis who claimed love and went to extremes in it, (Say, "If you should love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you") if you truly claim divine love, then why did you turn away from the Muhammadan guidance and innovate words of remembrance and sayings for which Allah sent down no authority, and contrive states that have no place in Islam?! (O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (28) (Al-Hadid) Throughout Surat al-Hadid (believe in Allah and His Messenger), except here He said (fear Allah) by being mindful of Him and in awe of Him unseen, (He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk) the reward is of the same kind as the deed: since they were mindful of Allah in all their states, He made for them a light like one walking with them, accompanying them everywhere, directing them, granting them success, helping them and giving them victory through it; so mercy is above the servant and light at his sides, like a companion who does not leave whoever has kept company with the Quran. So how could the devils of mankind and jinn, after this solid fortification, have any authority over one who has such protection and care from the Lord?! So the believer who fortified himself with the light of the Quran and was mindful of Allah in his private and public life has toiled in mindfulness and taken pains to keep this state of being mindful of Allah and knowing that He sees everywhere (and He is with you wherever you are), and the reward is that a double portion of mercy accompanies him, and light, everywhere And the verse from Surat Al-An'am explains it (And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never emerging therefrom? (122) He was dead and He gave him life with the Quran (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar), and reviving the heart from heedlessness is part of Allah's mercy (So observe the effects of the mercy of Allah — how He gives life to the earth after its death) (Ar-Rum), so it corresponds to His saying (He will give you a double portion of His mercy) (and made for him light by which to walk among the people) corresponds to (and make for you a light by which you will walk) So the meaning here in Al-Hadid is a light by which you walk within yourselves and among people "He mentioned the granting of light to the dead and said: by which to walk among the people, meaning: it accompanies him however he moves about; and He said: among the people, as an indication of its illuminating him himself and others among the people, so He mentioned that the believer's benefit is not confined to himself" (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar - from the tafsir of Al-An'am) So that the People of the Scripture may know that they are not able to obtain anything from the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty (29) He began the surah with the attributes and names of knowledge and power, and made clear their details throughout it: that He is able to revive hearts after their death through the Quran and soften them with humility, and that humility comes from being mindful of Allah and knowing that He is with the servant (and He is with you wherever you are), and also from not being deluded by the world so that it does not distract him from the remembrance of Allah and his daily portion of the Quran; and He closed it with this knowledge: that the bounty of guidance and the Book is in the hand of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills, because He is the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, and the possessor of great bounty.

t: (The flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight)
x: The lightning in Surah Al-Baqarah stands for the proofs of the Quran, in His words (The lightning almost snatches away their sight) (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar) The lightning in Surah Al-Baqarah stands for the proofs of the Quran, in His words (The lightning almost snatches away their sight) (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar) So the meaning of this verse in Surah An-Nur may be that the light of the Quran almost takes away the eyesight. The Quran, when it is recited, is not a single light! It is the light of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon the light of Jibril, peace be upon him, upon the light of Muhammad ﷺ, from whose blessed lips we received the Quran, upon the light of the angels who come to witness the Quran when it is recited, upon the light of the believer who recites it and listens to it (even if untouched by fire. Light upon light). The Quran's way is concision and omission, so it will not say: light upon light upon light upon light upon light! That would tire the reader. It is content to name two lights, and from them the reader grasps all the rest of those perfect lights. Even if untouched by fire: even if he had received no knowledge before it except the knowledge of the Quran, light would come to him, understanding would be complete in him, and every step of comprehension and ascent would be his. Have you not seen your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ? He received no learning, no books of religion or culture, before the Quran, and yet his knowledge reached beyond every horizon!? (And, [O Muhammad], you are not [engaged] in any matter or recite any of the Qur'an and you [people] do not do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it (61) (Yunus) He speaks generally of every matter and every deed: the angels guard it, write it and are present for it. But the Quran He singles out by name. And by Allah, He did not speak generally of every deed and matter and then single out the Quran from among them except for the greatness of its rank and station, and for the majesty of the Most Merciful and His angels bearing witness to it. Every matter and every deed is mentioned to warn, and to wake the sense of being watched; the Quran is mentioned to inspire longing and to exalt its station, for it stands above every matter. Working with it and being busy with it (reciting, listening, memorizing, explaining, pondering) is the greatest of the witnessed deeds kept in the record. It is what makes the believer's face shine and his whole countenance light up when he is handed his book in his right hand: his joy at finding his time with the Quran written in that record is greater than his joy at all his other deeds. It is the tremendous news that, for its greatness, the creatures of the heavens come to attend! Does this happen with the evening news? Does it happen with ordinary talk? Not at all. Those ordinary events are written by angels appointed to them (Allah knows best how many they are; in the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir they are two, perhaps four, and some said thirteen). But the Quran's station is greater: the angels come to witness it, calling to one another from every place, and spread their wings around the reciter, to his right and to his left, perhaps over his shoulder, while one angel places his lips upon the reciter's lips. Nothing so wondrous happens with ordinary things or with the other comings and goings of talk “When one of you gets up to pray at night, let him use the tooth-stick, for when one of you recites in his prayer, an angel places his mouth over his mouth, and nothing comes out of his mouth but it enters the angel's mouth” (its narrators are trustworthy) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The speech most beloved to Allah is the recitation of the Quran. Whoever sits down to recite it, the angels surround him with their wings, mercy covers them, and they are the guests of the Most Merciful until they plunge into some other talk” (weak) And reciting the Quran in a place brings blessing to it, brings down mercy upon it, and drives Satan out of it. “Al-Nawawi said: He urged that voluntary prayers be prayed at home only because that is more hidden and further from showing off, and so that the house may be blessed by it, mercy may descend in it, and Satan may flee from it.” That is the blessing of the Quran in a place; so tell me, by your Lord, what of the one who carries the Quran in the most hidden place of all: the heart! And this light is stronger than you imagine. Its power to drive away devils and to master the self and its flaws almost takes away the very breath and soul of those who recite, from the majesty of Allah the Almighty and the light of the angels. “What is wrong with those people who look towards the sky during the prayer? … They should stop (looking towards the sky during the prayer); otherwise their eyesight would be taken away” Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, may Allah have mercy on him, explained this hadith, saying: “And it was said that the meaning is: there is fear for their eyes from the lights with which the angels descend upon those who pray” The light of the Quran almost takes away the sight of the hypocrites and of the devils among men and jinn; and it almost takes away the sight of the believers. So if the light of the Quran is strong enough almost to take away keen, physical eyesight, what then of the darknesses and sins that every means has failed to erase, every stratagem has failed to remove or to guard against? And how could its meaning not shine out in the heart of the one who recites it, almost taking away eyes and all things of sense, until nothing is left in the place but light (Everyone upon the earth will perish). Yes indeed, the light of the Quran is fierce against the devils, fierce upon the heart, so fierce that it sweeps away the darknesses and comes down as light upon the servant: his heart is radiant, his deeds and words are light, and all around him, and his face, is a shining moon.

t: It Is Established That Prayers Are Answered When the Quran Is Completed
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: "It is authentically reported from the great Successor Mujahid ibn Jabr: "It is authentically reported from the great Successor Mujahid ibn Jabr: "Whoever completes the Quran is granted a prayer that is not turned away." And he also said: "It has reached us that prayers are answered when the Quran is completed. Imam al-Bukhari said: "With every completion comes an answered prayer" (Dr. Abdulaziz al-Shaya) "There are three whose prayers Allah does not turn away: the one who remembers Allah much, the one who has been wronged, and the just ruler" ( hasan ) And the Quran is the greatest remembrance of all (Sad. By the Qur'an containing reminder). Say "Subhan Allah" on its own, and you earn one good deed for it; but recite it from the Quran, and you earn ten good deeds for every letter, and every good deed is multiplied tenfold! (Dr. Ayman Suwayd) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stay up at night with Abu Bakr, talking over some matter of the Muslims' affairs. One night he stayed up with him, and I was with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out walking, and we went out walking with him, and there was a man standing in prayer in the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood listening to his recitation, and just as we were about to recognize the man, he said: "Whoever would love to recite the Quran fresh, as it was revealed, let him recite it as Ibn Umm Abd recites." He said: Then the man sat down to supplicate, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began saying: "Ask, and it will be given to you. Ask, and it will be given to you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for those who learn the Quran and the hadith by heart and pass them on: that their faces be radiant, and their prayers answered. "The Prophet ﷺ commanded his Ummah that those who were present should convey from him to those who were absent, and he prayed for those who convey with a prayer that is answered … He also said: "May Allah make radiant the face of a man who hears a hadith from us and conveys it to one who has not heard it. Many a bearer of knowledge is not himself a man of understanding, and many a bearer of knowledge carries it to one who understands it better than he. There are three things over which the heart of a Muslim harbors no rancor: sincerity of action for the sake of Allah, sincere counsel to those in authority, and holding fast to the community of the Muslims; for their supplication encompasses those behind them, . In this is a prayer from him for whoever conveys his hadith, even if he is not a man of understanding, and a prayer for whoever conveys it, even if the listener understands more than the one who conveys; because of the radiance granted to those who convey. That is why Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: You will not find a single one of the people of hadith but that there is radiance in his face, because of the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ" Ibn Taymiyyah

t: When the Spirit Expands, the Soul Opens Up
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: The psychological advice that says "Don't wait for your mood and feelings to improve; just start, and get to work anyway" is both right and wrong! The psychological advice that says "Don't wait for your mood and feelings to improve; just start, and get to work anyway" is both right and wrong! Right for the soul, and wrong for the spirit! Come, sit down here, and let's talk it through at our leisure; The advice is right for the soul: yes, whatever you feel, start and get to work. If laziness creeps up on you, and you yawn and drift off to sleep, where is the striving, where is the work? And if you answer to every passing feeling, where is your mastery over yourself, where is your victory? You must struggle, strain, and toil, and swim against your feelings and your whims. But it is wrong for the spirit; because the spirit comes from the breath of God, and it has a different nature and different moods, so the rules for handling it are somewhat different. For the heart first needs something to mend it before it can take in knowledge and set out to work. Once the spirit is restored and the breast expands, the heart opens up to the world and to everything in it: the appetite for food and drink returns; a person turns to others with his whole heart and listens with his ears, so he loves them and they love him; and the vessels of his mind widen to take in knowledge with a soul that is clear and whole. I was struck by the words of one contemporary Muslim philosopher, which I put in my own phrasing: "Whoever's spirit opens to the heavens opens to the earth; for opening to the Truth is opening to the creation. His mind opens to everything, and his heart to everyone. But when the vents of the spirit close, he shuts himself off from people, his appetite is shut off from food, and he hates and curses every corner of the world. For whoever is displeased with Allah, nothing in this world will ever please him" So if you ask me: and how is the spirit restored? We answer: open your night with the night prayer and witr, and begin it with the Quran, the heart's own food. Feed your hungry spirit. Fill it with food and nourishment and remembrance. Make it rich with the words of the Truth, so that it never goes begging from the creation! Fill it, fill it to the brim with the Quran, until it overflows and says: Enough, I am full, and now I am ready to face the world, whatever it may hold. "One-third, and even one-third is much. You'd better leave your inheritors wealthy rather than leaving them poor, begging others" (authentic hadith) And the inheritance left to you is the Quran: (Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants). So bequeath it to your spirit, until it is too rich to beg and keeps its hands to itself. As for the third, it is the third of the night with the Quran: an hour or two in which you weary your feet before your Master (Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muhammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it) (Al-Muzzammil: 20) And whoever does the opposite, beginning his day with people and the world, with no portion of Quran and no night prayer, has left himself open to the hardships of the day and whatever it brings. That's his lookout! Let him be! People play with him however they please: if they laugh, he laughs; if they grieve him, he grieves; he has no footing of his own. His understanding stumbles in his studies, his memory tires and grinds to a halt; the doors of the soul are bolted shut, and the windows of the senses refuse to let in the light. What hope can it have? His soul is sealed against taking anything in, tied up tight, until it sinks into gloom and falls flat on its face! Sealed off even from the loveliest, most delightful pastimes of his life, and from his most comforting friendships; because he began the wrong way around. (when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger) (At-Tawbah) "The disciples said: O Spirit of Allah, tell us of the one who is sincere to Allah. He said: The one who puts the right of Allah before the right of people; and when two matters come to him (or: when a matter of this world and a matter of the Hereafter present themselves to him), he begins with the one for the Hereafter, and then turns to the one for this world." (Ibn Kathir) So begin with the Hereafter, and from there go on to this world Come down from the spirit, and the soul will come along to you like a meek, quiet child in your hands: no mischief, no trouble, only obedience and response to one whose spirit has surrendered to the Truth, and so it yields and is spared the soul's troubles. (Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?) We expanded it with the Quran; and when the spirit expands, the soul opens up!

t: The People of the Quran Differ in Style and Manner
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: Some recite in slow, measured tartīl ; if they hurried, all the joy and delight would drain out of it, so they keep a small daily portion and draw great joy and delight from their tartīl . Some recite in slow, measured tartīl ; if they hurried, all the joy and delight would drain out of it, so they keep a small daily portion and draw great joy and delight from their tartīl . And some say: If I recited slowly, I'd fall asleep! I'd grow sluggish; nothing wakes me up like speed. And you will find them getting through a large daily portion. There was once a student just like this, who recited quickly. Her teacher told her to slow down and recite with tartīl : she lost her place and forgot! So the teacher let her be, speed and all. And this difference is perfectly fine! The reciter of the Quran is not to be blamed for it; he is simply guided, as far as he can manage, toward the middle way and moderation. The Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: "I passed by you while you were reciting and your voice was low." He said: "I made Him hear with Whom I was holding intimate converse." He said: "Raise your voice a little." Then he said to Umar: "I passed by you while you were reciting and your voice was loud." So he said: "I repel drowsiness and keep Ash-Shaitan away." So he said: "Lower your voice a little." - Sahih Now reflect! His prophetic guidance, (lower it a little) and (raise it a little), asked of them no great effort and nothing that would burden them. Nor did it ask them to change the temperament and human nature they were made with: some are slow by nature and some quick,,,. He simply guided and pointed them toward a little raising, a little lowering. And so should the teacher of the Quran be: mindful that human natures differ, and that every reciter has a temperament of their own. So leave them as they are; be gentle about it, and do not be harsh. Some are slow and some are fast, some loud and some soft.. Leave them to their nature, but guide them toward a little!

t: Swift Recitation (Hadr) and Reflection Are Not at Odds!
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: Reading many pages does not stand in the way of reflection and understanding. Reading many pages does not stand in the way of reflection and understanding. So said Dr. Saeed Hamza, an expert in Quran memorization, in his course The Secrets of Mastering Quran Memorization , and he gave a fine example: in Ramadan, the imams of the Two Holy Mosques in Makkah and Madinah recite the Taraweeh swiftly, in hadr ; yet a verse passes over their tongues and they weep at it, moved. Among those in our own time to whom understanding and reflection were opened wide was the engineer Muhammad al-Muqrami, may Allah have mercy on him, who used to complete the whole Quran every day and night; for him, taking in a great deal of the Quran never stood in the way of reflection and understanding. In fact, this idea is sometimes a whisper of Satan, meant to hold you back from gathering more good deeds and blessings: Make do with one page, reflection matters more! When in truth there is no conflict between the two. Read a juz' every day and it will be goodness and blessing whose mark and light you will see; and reflection, understanding and a corrected recitation will all come with time, Allah willing The best in the Prophetic Sunnah is to complete the Quran every month (a juz' a day), or every ten days (three juz'), or every seven (five juz'), or every three (ten juz'). One thing that makes it easier: spreading it across the five daily prayers. A single complete reading of the Quran holds three million good deeds, so let us not think little of it! May Allah bless us and you through the Mighty Quran and let us benefit from it.

t: The Effect of the Noble Quran on Mental and Physical Health
x: PubMed Central (PMC), the research archive of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), has published a study that brings together strong, reliable evidence on the effect of the Noble Quran on mental and physical health. It is titled: PubMed Central (PMC), the research archive of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), has published a study that brings together strong, reliable evidence on the effect of the Noble Quran on mental and physical health. It is titled: The Impact of Listening to, Reciting, or Memorizing the Quran on Physical and Mental Health of Muslims: Evidence From Systematic Review In it, the researchers gathered 230 studies published in major, high-ranking scientific databases, such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Nor did they take just any study: they selected them only after assessing their methodology and analyzing their data, to make sure the results were not the product of chance or bias. Then they organized the evidence and findings, and the results were astonishing: - Listening to Surah Ar-Rahman did much to help manage depression in pregnant women, and eased their anxiety about childbirth. - Listening to Surah Ya-Sin has a profound psychological effect on one's sense of calm and tranquility. - Listening to the Noble Quran in general reduced symptoms of depression and anxiety in kidney patients and heart patients. - Listening to the Quran improves sleep quality - Remarkably, when intensive care patients heard the Noble Quran, their vital-sign readings fell and their level of consciousness rose! - Listening to the Quran improves physiological markers (regulating heart rate, breathing..) - Listening to the Quran improves quality of life and average lifespan. - The Quran gives the mind bright, hopeful beliefs about life and about the events and hardships that befall it, making it steadier and stronger. - The more of the Quran one memorizes (surahs, juz', methods of review, and so on), the higher one's IQ. - Memorizing the Quran has a bearing on brain atrophy: gray matter, white matter, and total brain volume were larger in those who had memorized the whole Quran than in those who had not memorized it, or had memorized only part of it. The explanation is that the one who memorizes keeps using and stimulating brain tissue, which helps preserve it. On this matter, we recall the words of the Tabi'un, may Allah be pleased with them all: It is authentically reported that Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Whoever reads the Quran will not be returned to the most abject old age, and that is His saying: {Then We return him to the lowest of the low * Except for those who believe}; he said: except those who read the Quran. And from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said: It used to be said: Those whose minds stay sound the longest are the readers of the Quran” And al-Amin al-Shanqiti (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “It is widely and continuously attested, among common folk and scholars alike, that one who has memorized the Book of Allah and keeps up its recitation is not struck by dementia or delirium.

t: What Remains for a Person in His Darkest Hour?
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: So I wanted to share it, along with a few thoughts of my own: So I wanted to share it, along with a few thoughts of my own: Dr. Muhammad Hamza had memorized the Quran before he was thrown into prison, where the prisoners were forbidden to speak. He says he kept the Quran and taught it to his fellow prisoners by writing out each page in soap on black clothing, where the white lather shows up clearly against the dark, as it would not on colored clothes. With him in the cell was the writer and television screenwriter Adnan al-Zira'i, who memorized ten parts of the Book of Allah this way before he was martyred. He went on to tell how, in the last years of torture, his nerves were shattered and he hovered near death and sickness, so that reviewing the Quran in his head, from memory, grew slow: al-Baqarah, which used to take him half an hour, now took four or five. He felt his memory weakening, failing. And yet, he says, he was determined to keep his memory working and keep reviewing his daily portion, however much time and effort it cost him. And when he reached the words of the Exalted ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient, (155) Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." (156) Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided. (157) [Al-Baqarah: 155-157] the jailer came, called out his name, and gave him the good news of his release; and he walked out of prison after six lean years spent within its walls. What amazes me is that this man was a surgeon, healing the sick and performing operations, and at the same time a teacher of the Quran who carried it by heart. I don't know what to say as I listen to his story! Only that, while listening, I grasped one of the meanings of life and existence: when a person is cut off from everything, besieged by time and assailed from every side, denied his food and drink, his speech and his people, what remains with him!? Nothing but sorrows, and a memory that keeps replaying its pains. Nothing, unless he carries the Quran by heart. As he reviews his daily portion from memory, the words of the Quran crowd out the words of hatred, insult and abuse that are hurled at him, so he does not hurt, and does not much care what is aimed at him. That is why painful memories slip away from him easily, while his thoughts and mind are absorbed in going over the Quran. Memory, if you do not wear it out with memorizing and reviewing, will wear you out by memorizing sorrows and fears. That is when I recognized the root of a very modern affliction (overthinking): it is a memory emptied of its daily review of the Quran, so it fills itself with replaying the past, fretting over the future, chewing the same thoughts over and over. I have even come across the stories of many who, after memorizing the Quran and tending it through review and recitation, reported an astonishing thing: the intrusive whispers, the thoughts, the negative feelings vanished completely! Then I knew what remains for a person in his darkest hour: his own breast remains with him, and all he has entrusted to it of verses and recitations that heal him, tend to him, and bless his years. So what is left for the one who has not yet memorized it! And what is he waiting for!? As for those who object (understanding matters more than memorizing), I say: there are mathematical laws you cannot understand until you have repeated them and learned them by heart; with memorizing comes understanding. And so it is with the Quran. I remember a woman who wrote a post on Facebook: she had resolved to memorize the Quran, and a friend asked her, "Why memorize it? Reflecting on it matters more than memorizing it." And now, she wrote, the years have gone by, and I have neither memorized it nor reflected on it. So, my friend, no companion will stay by your side in hardship but the Quran. It is the springtime and it is the rain; learn it by heart, and you will find in it companionship and joy. I ask Allah the Exalted to make the Quran the springtime of our hearts, and to make memorizing it easy for me and for you, in pardon and well-being, in peace and safety. From the book (Ya Bushra Hadha Ghulam)

t: Creative Ways to Understand the Quran
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: Creative ways to understand the Quran (mix them up, and taste the delight of understanding and reflection): Creative ways to understand the Quran (mix them up, and taste the delight of understanding and reflection): - When a verse crosses your mind and won't let you go, don't brush it aside. Believe me, it's a message! Go and look up its tafsir. - Give great care to the parables and stories of the Quran. One of the early Muslims used to weep whenever he recited (And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge), afraid that he might not be one of those of knowledge! - Each time, pick a group of verses on a single theme (the story of the People of the Cave, the verses on riba, the five verses of Surat al-Baqarah...), look up their tafsir, sum them up, and share them with a friend or on your page. - Tafsir in a nutshell: the rare words, the meaning of the verse, the occasion of revelation, what abrogates and what is abrogated, and the lessons for reflection and action. - I advise you to read your daily portion in one of the short, simplified tafsirs - When you come across a word you don't know, look it up in the Mushaf al-Madinah app, and turn on the feature that colours the rare words and shows their meanings. Word by word, day after day, you will suddenly find that you know the meanings of most of the words! And a great door of reflection will have swung open for you. - Grab a friend and say: quiz me on the meanings of the words! - Share what you learn with others: talk it over with a friend, post it on your page. - The apps I recommend: al-Tafsir al-Muharrar, Mushaf al-Madinah, al-Tafsir al-Tafa'uli (audio), Tadarus al-Quran (amazing!)

t: The People of Allah Catch the Scent of Hearts
x: The people of Allah catch the scent of hearts from miles away, and they feel it in their own hearts as a contraction or an expansion. The people of Allah catch the scent of hearts from miles away, and they feel it in their own hearts as a contraction or an expansion. (Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that Allah would never expose their [feelings of] hatred) Do the hypocrites imagine that Allah will not lay their affair bare before His believing servants? Rather, He will make it plain and bring it to light, until those of insight understand them. (Ibn Kathir) And what good are light and insight — those very things you have chattered to us about so endlessly? (O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion) He left "criterion" unqualified and general, and left its object unstated, so that it would embrace everything: a criterion in every matter of this world and the Hereafter. By it the ambiguous is recognized, the knotty is untied, distress is lifted, enemies are routed, and darkness is extinguished beneath the light of humble devotion and the cloak of good deeds; and through it come wondrous powers of discernment that tell the enemy apart from the friend. And insight — and what will make you know what insight is? It lets you hear the greetings within the heart and its hidden longings, and the subtle things that stir it; it shows you the stories behind the walls. Its light in the heart cannot be resisted; it rises in might and prevails. It guides your steps, until you hear all sorts of stories: "I don't know what made me get up right then?!" "No idea why I went to that place.." I don't know! But Allah knows, and He makes it known to the people of knowing and of faith: He turns their hearts and their feet toward safe shores in the hours of evil, and shows them His gentleness and how He deals with their enemy, so that they watch the crime scene, and their own part in the play, from afar — praising, stunned, marvelling, safe, gazing up at the sky and saying: Alhamdulillah! You have never once forsaken us! Abashed before such gentle graces. From this they grew addicted to the love of the Beloved; from this they kept their eyes upon their mushafs; from here they never wearied of the sweetness of standing before Him once the lamp was put out — for a lamp rose over them, shining from their inmost selves to their outward selves. "Whenever I said that nearness would put out the fires in my heart, union only fanned the blaze — such is the lover's lot. In union I find no solace, nor does parting make me forget; for love there is no cure, so count your mind and soul as lost. I have yielded up my fate to love, in meaning and in sense. Ah, my heart torn to pieces! Ah, my slaying and my plunder! I died of those gentle graces — such is the lover's lot." So, O forsaken one! You picked the wrong enemy. You are the forsaken one, not they.

t: How Do You Build a House Stronger Than the Spider's House?
x: Surat al-Ankabut began with striving against the self (And whoever strives only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds (6) (Al-Ankabut) Surat al-Ankabut began with striving against the self (And whoever strives only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds (6) (Al-Ankabut) And it ended with striving (And those who strive for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good (69) (Al-Ankabut) The surah has not ended yet! For after it came: (Alif, Lam, Meem (1) The Byzantines have been defeated (2) In the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome (3) Within three to nine years. To Allah belongs the command before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice (4) In the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful (5) [It is] the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know (6) (Ar-Rum) Striving against the self in obedience and in leaving sin: a road whose beginning is trials (Alif, Lam, Meem. Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried? (2) But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars (3)(Al-Ankabut) Do those on their way to their Lord think they will not be tried and tested!? No, rather the one who is truthful in his claim must be distinguished from the one who lies. If there were a programmer's job and 2,000 applicants came for it, each claiming to be the best, wouldn't it be fair for the hiring manager to test their abilities and claims, by putting a computer in front of them and saying: You're a programmer? Let me see your work! And test him on the program. And to Allah belongs the highest example: if everyone who said "I am a believer and righteous" were taken at their word, everyone would enter Paradise! There has to be a process of filtering and sorting, and intensive, successive tests, from a hard test to a harder one; all of this for the quality of the sorting and then the choosing, for the Most Merciful does not choose just anyone for His abode, but those who passed the tests with success and distinction. And there are those whose selves grew too weak to strive, and who turned back on their heels His weakness in striving is like the weakness of the spider's house, for her house is the frailest: the weakest, and I also see in the meaning lowliness, humiliation, and smallness; if you blew on it, all she built would be gone. (The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if they only knew (41) (Al-Ankabut) And part of the heart's weakness is that if good befalls it, it rejoices and says Allah loves me, and if a calamity befalls it, it abandons what it was upon (And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah," but when one [of them] is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, they consider the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they say, "Indeed, We were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all creatures? (10) And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites (11) (Al-Ankabut) And the strength of the believer's heart lies in his being one and the same in all conditions, devoted to the One, neither changing nor shifting The states of time upon you are many and varied Yet your state is one in every state (al-Mutanabbi) Why do you think Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, placed the story of Noah and Abraham (peace be upon them) in Surat al-Ankabut? Because their building is lofty and firm. Before you is Noah (peace be upon him), who was patient for a thousand years minus fifty, an example to follow in strength of heart and long endurance: (And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers (14) But We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds (15) (Al-Ankabut) And the self never weakens the way it weakens over the matter of provision! A person may be among the most devoted of people in worship and the most knowledgeable, yet the matter of provision keeps him up at night, and it is the reason he abandons all kinds of striving! So when provision comes to him, he leaves the recommended deeds he used to do and perhaps falls short in the obligatory ones, and if he finds it slow in coming, he says: My Lord has humiliated me! And because provision is the most important standard by which Allah distinguishes the truthful from the liar, He makes it come late! So that there is a period of refining and testing, sufficient and complete, to distinguish the believer from the hypocrite (And [We sent] Abraham, when he said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know (16) You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you produce a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned." (17) (Al-Ankabut) Whoever does not understand this road will be greatly delayed and even more shaken. Among them are those who despaired and lost hope because of delayed provision and the many trials, so they abandoned striving and said: This is nothing but legends of the former peoples. (And the ones who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and the meeting with Him — those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment (23) (Al-Ankabut) And among them are those given the resolve of Abraham (peace be upon him), so they were patient and strove until Allah saved them by His grace and generosity (And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe (24) (Al-Ankabut) And I picture this scene: Abraham (peace be upon him) came out of the fire and carried on calling to Allah the Exalted! As if nothing had happened. That is why this verse came after it: (And [Abraham] said, "You have only taken, other than Allah, idols as [a bond of] affection among you in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers." (25) (Al-Ankabut) And among the most important signs of striving: emigration ( hijrah ), by forsaking every evil you were settled in, whether beliefs, ideas, behaviors, relationships, or surroundings. And know that emigration is very costly, and without it the truthful cannot be distinguished from the liar! So whoever strives for Allah as He deserves must take up the worship of leaving, not obedience alone: “The emigrant is the one who forsakes evil deeds” “the one who forsakes what Allah has forbidden” and in one wording he said “the one who forsakes evil.” Emigration and sacrifice are among the hardest of tests: that you leave what you love for the sake of a greater Beloved (And Lot believed him. [Abraham] said, "Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." (26) (Al-Ankabut) (O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me (56) (Al-Ankabut) My earth is spacious: sins have substitutes among acts of obedience, gossip and idle talk have a replacement in beneficial knowledge, a bad friend is replaced by a righteous friend, goodness and mercy, and better and more ample than unlawful money is lawful, blessed money. You do not leave anything but that something more beautiful and more beneficial takes its place; (And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many locations and abundance) (An-Nisa) It is as if repentance and striving are a journey and a voyage to a more beautiful city, a roomier and more spacious place than the one you lived in. And the reward for all that patience and that hardship and striving: (And We gave to him Isaac and Jacob and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture. And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous (27).(Al-Ankabut) And in this verse He placed the greatest aid to striving, especially to forsaking sins: reciting the Quran, and prayer (Recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do (45) (Al-Ankabut) Then He mentioned the merit of the one who memorizes the Quran: that his house is firmer in piety, and it is the strongest and sturdiest of houses: (Rather, it [i.e., the Quran] is distinct verses [preserved] within the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers (49) (Al-Ankabut) And the one who has nothing of the Quran inside him to recite and memorize is toyed with by whispers, and the slightest passing thought shakes his steadiness and certainty; desires lead him astray, doubts assassinate him, devils make things seem fair to him, and everything plays with his emotions. And the problem is that he does not know that the cause of his heart's sickness and his self's weakness is his distance from the Quran; whoever forsakes the Quran, evil does not forsake him: “Indeed, the one who has nothing of the Quran inside him is like the ruined house” But the one who has a daily portion of the Quran and memorizes some of it, you find his house among the strongest of houses and the firmest in standing; his richness is in his heart, and his sufficiency endures through his Lord (And is it not sufficient for them that We revealed to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe (51) (Al-Ankabut) "Whoever's beginning shines, his end shines" Whoever's beginning shines with striving and repentance, his end shines by his becoming one of the doers of good And it ended with striving (And those who strive for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good (69) (Al-Ankabut) Imam al-Ghazali (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Upon the servant is to take up the means of striving (And those who strive for Us) and upon Allah is guidance (We will surely guide them to Our ways) And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good: those who strove; He named their striving: doing good ( iḥsān )! And Allah is with the doer of good by His companionship, protection, and support, and that is why after Surat al-Ankabut came: Ar-Rum (Alif, Lam, Meem (1) The Byzantines have been defeated (2) In the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome (3) Within three to nine years. To Allah belongs the command before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice (4) In the victory of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful (5) [It is] the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know (6) (Ar-Rum) By Allah, whoever strove against himself has won! He has won against the enemies of the self, against whims, and against the devils among men and jinn! This feeling of great victory is sweeter than all the certificates he has earned and the achievements he has reaped, something indescribable! He feels he is a king walking the earth, and a bright star in the sky! The one who has won against himself is worthy of winning against the outside enemy, however great its strength: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "You do not defeat your enemy by numbers, nor by equipment, but you defeat them by this religion; so if you and your enemy become equal in sins, victory will be theirs" So build a strong house whose beginning is striving and whose end is striving, then doing good, then victory.

t: The Importance of Reciting and Memorizing the Quran
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: Reciting and memorizing the Quran matter because they bind the heart to the Most Merciful; the love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is won through abundant remembrance, and whoever loves something speaks of it often. Reciting and memorizing the Quran matter because they bind the heart to the Most Merciful; the love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is won through abundant remembrance, and whoever loves something speaks of it often. And understanding the Quran matters because it helps you live by it; the measure of your understanding is the measure of your practice: A narrow understanding, a meager practice. A broad understanding, an abundant practice. Allah has shown us why the Children of Israel killed their prophets, and why they denied, disbelieved, and mocked: they read the Torah as mere words without grasping it, and so they did not live by it. He said: (And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking). That is: they recite its words, but its meanings escape them.

t: Reason Does Not Come From Many Books
x: The frontal lobe, the seat of logic and rational decision-making: neuroscience has found that it grows the more a person masters his emotions and feelings. It expands through will and choice, just as it expands and grows each time we feed it something useful. The frontal lobe, the seat of logic and rational decision-making: neuroscience has found that it grows the more a person masters his emotions and feelings. It expands through will and choice, just as it expands and grows each time we feed it something useful. Reason does not come from many books; reason is holding your soul back from its cravings and its whims. In the Arabic language, ʿaql (reason) means restraint. The person of reason, then, is the one who has held his soul back from its desires. Go, if you like, and learn logic, statistics, programming, every intricate science; master each one until you have worn it threadbare. A part of your reason will still be missing until you learn the Quran and the Sunnah, and labor to refine your soul and cleanse it of whisperings and stray thoughts until it is whole and undivided, surrendered to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Among the names of the Quran is al-Muḥkam , from ḥukm , the governing of oneself. And so the Quran is the finest help a person can have, after the grace of Allah the Exalted, in learning will, restraint, discipline, and mastery of the self.

t: The Righteous Friend
x: The righteous friend wants you for your Lord, not for himself, The righteous friend wants you for your Lord, not for himself, he seeks no advantage and asks you for no money; his whole bond with you turns on obedience: obey, and he draws you close; disobey, and he reproaches you; and if you will not stop, he keeps his distance. Know, then, that he is saving you for the Hereafter, and has no need of your worldly life. He lifts your resolve toward the heights and walks there beside you when determination flags and aspiration falters; he prays for you, and his prayers for you are answered. And in the Hereafter he will be with you on pulpits of light, for which the prophets and the martyrs will envy you. Not every prophet has a righteous friend; some of them will be raised alone on the Day of Resurrection. And the friend intercedes for the believers, and for those he knew in this world, once Allah grants permission and is pleased with him, and he is the anguish of the disbelievers, who say in the Fire, with a moan that tears at the heart, (So now we have no intercessors and not a devoted friend. Then if we only had a return [to the world] and could be of the believers): if only I were sent back to life and became a believer honored by Allah, so that I could intercede — or, at the very least, a righteous friend who knows me and whom I know, to intercede for me! This provision comes from your Lord alone, so if you have been denied it, ask Him and call upon Him, and do not lose heart or grow weary: say, O Allah, grant me and make easy for me good and righteous companions, with whom I will sit on pulpits of light on the Day of Resurrection. O people, listen and understand, and know that Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and the martyrs envy for their rank and their nearness to Allah. Then a Bedouin from the far edge of the gathering knelt down, gestured with his hand toward the Prophet ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah: people among the people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, yet the prophets and the martyrs envy them for their places and their nearness [to Allah]? Describe them to us, portray them for us — that is, tell us what they are like. The Prophet's face lit up with joy at the Bedouin's question, and he said: They are people from among the obscure of humanity and strangers drawn from different tribes, bound by no close ties of kinship; they loved one another for the sake of Allah and were sincere toward one another. On the Day of Resurrection Allah will set up for them pulpits of light, and they will sit upon them, and He will make their faces light and their garments light. The people will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection, but they will not be terrified, and they are the allies of Allah: there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. A hasan hadith

t: The Sprout: On the Means of Holding Firm to Guidance Until Death —by the Leave of Allah the Exalted—
x: I know! You live in dread of slipping after you have walked straight; it buzzes in your head like a bee, on and on… When that thought comes, do nothing and do not overthink it; just say: “O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.” I know! You live in dread of slipping after you have walked straight; it buzzes in your head like a bee, on and on… When that thought comes, do nothing and do not overthink it; just say: “O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.” Leave guidance to its Owner, hand the keys to its Keeper, and what an excellent Keeper He is. Yes, steadfastness comes from Allah the Exalted, yet the servant must take up its means #strive: Do not sit with the people of falsehood who make you doubt the truth of faith in Allah and the Last Day. Do not listen to them. Do not say, “It won’t affect me.” Oh, it will: your certainty in the Hereafter slips a notch or two, and then you can barely lift it back up. So are you ready to lift it again after every single drop!? I am not ready! Then do not listen to them. If you come across lines that cast doubt on the foundations of the faith, do not play the virtuoso and say (I’ll take it on, let me read what it says! Why all these restrictions? I can refute it..) We have been told of a man who knew whole texts of fiqh by heart and could recite them without pause; he exposed himself to the doubts of the atheists, and they lodged in his heart and would not leave, until he became an atheist, after having been a proud believer in the One God —O Allah, we ask You for safety—. So here is advice from the heart: do not take them on, so long as this is not your field. I am no specialist in answering doubts; so why would I expose myself to them!? Why, when the daylight is plain before him, does he ask like a fool: Does the sun exist or not? Do not turn your faith into a playground for every passerby to toy with as he pleases, wrecking years of certainty that you built and labored over! Have you ever seen a man with wealth and standing who, in a single second, tore down everything he had built, until nothing was left!
