Such is his likeness (Whoever makes his religion a target for disputes will keep shifting from one thing to another) A man came to al-Hasan al-Basri and said: O Abu Sa‘id, I want to dispute with you. He said: (Keep away from me; I know my religion. It is only one who doubts his religion who would dispute with you) And Malik ibn Anas, whenever one of the people of whims came to him, would say: (As for me, I stand on clear proof from my Lord; as for you, you are in doubt, so go to a doubter like yourself and dispute with him) A man from among the people of innovation came to debate him, and Malik said: (They confuse themselves, then go looking for someone to set them straight) ( Al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah , commentary by Prof. Dr. Khalid al-Muslih) (See an earlier article of ours explaining the words of Allah the Exalted (And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them..) And among the causes of swerving after guidance: 1- Putting reason ahead of revealed knowledge and faith. 2- Personal vanity, and a haughty refusal to accept facts, evidence, and proofs. 3- Drifting back and forth in doubt without taking up the means of certainty. Among what increases certainty: revealed knowledge; learning the deeds and the understanding of the heart, so that faith and devotion to Allah take root; and humility before the truth when it appears. 4- Being dazzled by the adornment of this worldly life. Keep the world in your hand (by taking the means and making the effort required) and not in your heart, lest you cling to it and crave it. This is the finest definition of zuhd , and the sign that the heart has renounced the world is that losing something does not grieve you, nor does its arrival make you rejoice; rather, falling short in obedience grieves you, and fulfilling it brings you joy. And the answer: No, you are not shielded from influence the way the angels are; you are a human being, who moves others and is moved by them. So do not say: My mind can handle hearing the stories and the news, watching the pictures and the videos, and none of it touches me. Oh, it does; your mind is touched without even knowing it. Do not say, “I love to confront, not to run away”; sometimes running is the only way a drowning man escapes the water, and we have been commanded to flee from the lion: “one should run away from the leper as one runs away from a lion.” How many a man was undone by his own courage! {And do not kill yourselves}. Have you not seen that the master of the brave, Muhammad, upon him be blessings and peace, was commanded to keep away from sitting with the people of falsehood, and this though he was protected from error! He did not say, “I am a Prophet; it won’t affect me.” {And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation}. Have you not seen that Yusuf, Prophet and Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), fled from the wife of al-Aziz? {And they both raced to the door}. We were told of a righteous man who heard the story of someone falling into a sin, and it gripped him so fiercely that he committed the sin himself! And all it was, was a story, something he heard! {And [it is] so the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter will incline toward it and that they will be satisfied with it and that they will commit that which they are committing} Dr. Ahmad Abdel-Moneim said: This verse lays out the stages of people’s fall into temptation —the steps of being influenced—: 1- Inclining (listening) 2- Being satisfied with what they heard, with no rejection of it in the heart 3- The act and the deed. I say: the stronger one’s faith in Allah and in the unseen, the stronger the heart stands when it hears temptation, and the firmer it holds against doubt and desire. Yet however high faith may climb, one must still flee and not listen. Have you not seen that even the heroes and fearless champions of war are commanded to lower their gaze! And is lowering the gaze not a way of running away! And so the question was: Can a person resist being influenced?

t: Heavenly Standing
x: Imagine setting your heart on standing, on a lofty and praiseworthy name, among the dwellers of heaven! Imagine setting your heart on standing, on a lofty and praiseworthy name, among the dwellers of heaven! Seek distinction! Distinction in the sight of Allah the Exalted (And he, in the sight of Allah, was distinguished) wajīhan (“distinguished”): one whose prayer is heard, who is never forsaken, whose hope is never dashed and whose word never falls to the ground. Have you seen all the arts of fame, of building a social standing, of winning people's affection? Had you invested them in heaven, it would have been far better for you! Better than spending them on people whom nothing about you will ever please. "Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: O Allah, make me in Your sight among the highest of Your creation, in my own eyes among the lowliest of Your creation, and in the eyes of people among the middling of Your creation" (Ibn Kathir)

t: Surat an-Nur Shows Us How to Reach the Light
x: To have the light of Allah reach the heart of His believing servant, you do not need endless prayer and fasting; it is simpler than that. These three are enough for you: To have the light of Allah reach the heart of His believing servant, you do not need endless prayer and fasting; it is simpler than that. These three are enough for you: 1- Purifying your hearing 2- Purifying your tongue 3- Purifying your sight And the light will come, if Allah wills! The surah opens with just two verses on the familiar indecency of the deed (verses 2-3), and twenty-three on the many kinds of indecency of the tongue! (4-26) As if to tell us that the indecency of the tongue is far graver than we imagine: we make light of it, but Allah says it is tremendous! (When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge and thought it was insignificant while it was, in the sight of Allah, tremendous (15) [An-Nur] The kinds of indecency of the tongue in the surah: 1- Accusing chaste, unsuspecting women, and likewise chaste, unsuspecting believing men, with no proof and no witnesses. 2- Spouses accusing one another with no proof and no witnesses. 3- The lying slander, the fabrications against the honor of people who are wholly innocent. 4- Thinking ill of believing men and women and casting doubt on their honor without evidence or witness, out of nothing but whim; and this Allah the Exalted called a manifest slander. 5- Wading into people's honor even when there is proof and evidence and the thing truly happened. Are you a judge? Are you a witness holding evidence? The answer is no! Then why wade into their honor, even if it happened and the news is true? What business is it of yours? Look to your own soul and weep over your own sin. We have known people who waded into the honor of others, gloating and mocking, only to fall into the very thing they had fallen into. So take heed, and beware: this is not the character of one who comes to his Lord with a sound heart. "By Allah, O Hazzal, had you covered him with your garment, it would have been better than what you did to him" Narrated by Imam Ahmad Imam Malik said: "In this town (meaning Madinah) I knew people who had no faults; they found fault with others, and so came to have faults. And in this town I knew people who had faults; they kept silent about the faults of others, and so their own faults were forgotten" So cover the faults of Muslim men and women, and Allah will cover yours in this world and the Hereafter. The cure lies in what the verse says (And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You, [O Allah]; this is a great slander."?) [An-Nur] Its meaning: why, when you heard such reports, did you not hold your peace and keep out of them, and say: Glory be to You! This is false talk; it is not for us to let our tongues speak of it, or our suspicions turn it over, or to mention it to anyone. Glory be to You, our Lord; we declare You far above this monstrous lie! Ibn Kathir said: (This is a second lesson in manners after the first, which was the command to think well of others: that is, when something unbecoming is said about the best of people, then all the more should one think well of them, and not let oneself feel anything else; and if something of it should still cling to the soul (a whisper or a passing fancy), one should not speak of it). So the verses teach us to purify our hearing from listening to such rumors and reports (even when they are true): not to browse them, not to comment on them, but to pass them by with dignity, for this is a trait of the servants of the Most Merciful (and when they pass near ill speech, they pass by with dignity); and to purify the tongue and our suspicions, speaking of believing men and women only with good, and thinking well of them. 6- Swearing too much! A person should not swear oaths often, and should rid himself of idle oaths as far as he can; it is disliked, and some even counted it a mark of hypocrisy. My father once told us of a friend of his who had gone many years without swearing by Allah even once! I said: now that is true honor! (And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear..) (An-Nur) Lā yaʾtali : let him not swear. 7- Pardoning and overlooking whoever has assailed others' honor, if he repents, turns back, and does not persist in what he said (And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (22) The outcome: (Evil words are for evil men, and evil men are [subjected] to evil words. And good words are for good men, and good men are [an object] of good words. Those [good people] are declared innocent of what the slanderers say. For them is forgiveness and noble provision.) [An-Nur] The more a person cleanses himself of foul speech and purifies his hearing and his tongue, the purer and more chaste he becomes, and the more worthy of chastity and goodness (The ones whom the angels take in death, [being] good and pure). They kept their speech and their hearing clean of filth and of trespassing on people's honor, so Allah made their words good and sweet at the hour of death; these are the ones who truly deserve to be called good. And it is this goodness that makes him fit for the light to enter the depths of his heart and his innermost being, even if he never toiled at endless prayer and fasting “They said: O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so fasts by day and prays by night, but she harms her neighbors? He said: She is in the Fire. They said: O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so prays only the obligatory prayers and gives in charity pieces of dried curd, but she does not harm her neighbors? He said: She is in Paradise” - Sahih And this shows that whoever thinks ill of people, wades into their honor, listens to such talk, believes it and repeats it, is foul, be it a foul man or a foul woman. "This is proof that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, clears the family of a good and chaste man of foulness; for good women are for good men and good men for good women. And this is part of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: the more good, clean and pure a person is, the more Allah, Glorified and Exalted, prepares for him a family of the same standing, a fitting recompense; and the reverse holds if he is foul, especially in matters of chastity. And this is what we usually see in reality: a man of foul character has a family like him, because he did not guard himself, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not guard him" (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar) "Evil words are for evil men, and evil men are for evil words; and good words are for good men, and good men are for good words. That is: the evil words the hypocrites attributed to Aisha are more fitting for them, and she is more fitting for innocence and purity than they are; and so the Exalted said: Those [good people] are declared innocent of what the slanderers say [An-Nur: 26]," (Ibn Kathir). And part of guarding the hearing, the tongue and the sight is that He laid down the etiquette of asking permission before entering, so that a person's eye does not fall on what he would hate to see, of his own family or of others. Allah the Exalted does not only forbid the act itself; He forbids even drawing near to it (But do not approach this tree) (And do not approach the orphan's property..) (which is abrogated), (And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse..). (But do not approach this tree): He stressed the prohibition and made it all the stronger by first forbidding them to go near it, before forbidding them the act itself (the eating). For merely drawing near, seeing and hearing, is enough to make the sin look lovely in the heart and make a person fond of it. He forbade drawing near, and forbade every path that leads to sin; a person wrongs himself simply by drawing near it, by nothing more than drawing near "Nearness to a thing breeds an urge and an inclination that seize the whole heart; this is what familiarity brings, and familiarity invites love, so that one sees nothing ugly and hears no prohibition, and it distracts him from what revelation and reason require. For He made their approaching the tree a cause of their being among the wrongdoers; and a cause that invites to evil is forbidden, just as a cause that leads to good is commanded" (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar) 3- Purifying the sight: He commanded believing men and women to lower their gaze, for this is a means of attaining goodness and chastity. And He gave believing women etiquettes that help keep the gaze, the speech and the hearing pure. As for hearing: "let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment", that is, a woman striking the anklet on her foot so that a man will hear it. And He commanded her to wear the hijab, which keeps the gaze pure. And He commanded whoever cannot find the means to marry to stay chaste and pure until Allah enriches him and provides for him. He must take up the means of chastity and strive in them: fasting often, lowering the gaze and all that was mentioned before, and filling his time with knowledge and useful pursuits instead of dwelling on this matter, not letting it occupy his mind too much. Haven't you heard that Imam al-Nawawi was asked: When will you marry? And he said: I forgot all about it! Meaning, it was simply not on his mind, so absorbed was he in knowledge. And Ibn Kathir said about the words of the Exalted (But let them who find not [the means for] marriage abstain [from sexual relations] until Allah enriches them from His bounty) this is the man who has no wife: "let him gaze upon the dominion of the heavens and the earth until Allah enriches him."! So when he has done all this, purified his hearing, his sight and his tongue, and kept chaste, his heart is cleansed and becomes more fit for the light of Allah to enter it. And what is the light of Allah? It is the Quran! (And We have certainly sent down to you distinct verses and examples from those who passed on before you and an admonition for those who fear Allah (34) Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things (35)) Admonition: that which holds one back from sin. Emptying comes before adorning: once a person has emptied himself, purified and cleansed himself of the causes of indecency in word and deed, and kept away from them, he is the most worthy of the light of Allah and of holding fast to the Quran. And once the light has settled in his heart, he spreads light wherever he goes: ([Such niches are] in mosques which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein; exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings [are] men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah. They fear a Day in which the hearts and eyes will [fearfully] turn about) (An-Nur) The verses show the fruit of this light: the believer now prefers the Hereafter to this world, his heart grows tender, humble and lowly before Allah the Exalted, and fear, awe and hope come to dwell in it. These lofty qualities are reached in no other way! Purity of hearing, sight and tongue, then the light of Allah, the Quran, until he reaches the fruits of the light and spreads it among people (And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people). This light is the Quran: it lit up his heart, and then it shone on those around him. So the believer's light is inward, real and deep-rooted, rising from his heart and then lighting up all around him; while the hypocrite's light is outward, with no root in the heart, as the verses of Surat al-Baqarah show (Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him). The hypocrite borrowed from another to kindle his light, and it lit up the outside, not his heart, as al-Tafsir al-Muharrar explains. Then He describes the state of the one who is its very opposite: (Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light (40) (An-Nur) Whoever is foul in speech, in hearing and in sight, the very opposite of those qualities, lives in darkness of heart upon darkness of place, spreading foul words. How would Allah grant light to one who never took up the means of light! Whoever reflects on Surat an-Nur will find it full of words kin to light! Flash, lightning, sight (The flash of its lightening almost takes away the eyesight. Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision). Allah is able to bring the servant out of darkness into light, and the reverse, according to whether he takes up or abandons the means of light. And there are means of steadfastness the servant must strive for, so that his heart is not turned about as the night and the day are turned about: “A man would be a believer in the morning and an unbeliever in the evening, or he would be a believer in the evening and an unbeliever in the morning, and would sell his faith for a paltry worldly gain” Then He crowns all this with obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and contentment with their rulings, while the hypocrite is the very opposite; and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and lives in awe of Him has won the prize (And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him - it is those who are the attainers (52) (An-Nur) And once he has passed through these stages, Allah, by His leave, establishes him in the land: (Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient (55) (An-Nur) How could he be established in the land when he has not cleansed himself of foul speech and of a roaming gaze? He will be someone others follow, and such traits do not befit him. The cleansing must come first, so that the establishing may come after! And notice that He calls whoever goes back to the darkness after being established in the land fāsiq , defiantly disobedient! “Abusing a Muslim is fusūq .” Purify the inner self through the hearing, the tongue and the sight; then the light settles in the heart and he holds fast to the Quran; then he spreads the light, and stands firm in obedience to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ; and so he is established in the land, if Allah wills. Whoever reflects on the surah will find it repeating again and again (And Allah is Hearing and Knowing) (And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing), driving home that Allah hears your words; so beware of what you say and what you do, for He hears it all and knows it all, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. And whoever keeps watch over himself before the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing receives a fitting reward: the All-Encompassing, the All-Knowing widens for him his religion and his world, and increases him in light.

t: What Is the Difference Between Thinking (Fikr) and Reasoning ('Aql)?
x: One of the leading voices in reflecting on the verses (and one I love to listen to) was asked by the presenter: Why, in Surat Ar-Ra'd, do we find (Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought), and in An-Nahl (Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought), and why (Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason) in both surahs? One of the leading voices in reflecting on the verses (and one I love to listen to) was asked by the presenter: Why, in Surat Ar-Ra'd, do we find (Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought), and in An-Nahl (Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought), and why (Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason) in both surahs? He answered that (for a people who reason) belongs to the signs of the heavens, and for a people who give thought to the signs of the earth. I said: There is a contradiction here that no one could miss! For in Surat Ar-Ra'd, both thinking ( tafakkur ) and reasoning ( taʿaqqul ) come with the signs of the earth! That is not the answer, because that is not the question: What is the difference between "signs" and "a sign"..: The real question is: Why do they come in this same order in three surahs, Ar-Ra'd, An-Nahl and Ar-Rum: for a people who give thought, then for a people who reason? And what is the difference between thinking and reasoning? We say (and it is Allah whose help is sought): What sets thinking and reasoning apart in the Quran is negation. Negation? Yes. Look: the Quran says (and most of them do not reason). Yet there is not a single verse in the whole Quran that denies people thought: (they do not give thought)! And what does that mean? I believe (and true knowledge is with Allah) that it means thinking is an instinctive, natural ability in human beings: every human being thinks, but not everyone who thinks reasons. Thinking is one and the same material in everyone (I do not mean physical material, but its kind), whereas reasoning is not found in everyone. Thinking stands at a single level; reasoning rises by many degrees, each person's reason taking shape according to his effort, his surroundings, his culture and his society. Thinking does not bend to nature or to outside forces. For thinking is instinctive, and reasoning is acquired. No one can tear thinking out of a person; but his reason is shaped by others, and shapes them in turn. Thinking tends to hold still; reasoning tends to change. Thinking is the ability to observe, to remember, to retain, to pay attention, to concentrate, and so on; it is our inner talk, our feelings and emotions, our imaginings and memories. Reasoning is using all of these, and steering them, soundly and rightly. Have you not seen how some people think, yet come out with wrong conclusions and wrong ideas? Yes, he thought; but he did not reason. And if he thinks and arrives at sound results? Then he is one who thinks and reasons. And if you ask me: Which is more bound up with the physical (the brain), thinking or reasoning? I would answer: thinking is closer to the brain than reasoning is. Do you not see that Allah the Exalted says (Then will you not hear?) (Then will you not see?), and does not say: Will you not walk? Will you not use your hands? Why? Because hearing and sight are the nearest to the brain and to thinking. So "Will you not hear?" means: will you not set your reason to work on what you hear, and so understand what is said!? Will you not reason about what you see? For what the Quran seeks from sight and hearing is that we think about what they bring in, then reason, and so find our way to the truth. Sight and reason and hearing are of no use if they do not bring their owner to the truth; that is the whole point. That is why He said: (And among them are those who listen to you. But can you cause the deaf to hear, although they will not use reason (42) [Yunus] They listen to the Quran, but they do not reason about what they hear; so there is no difference between them and the deaf. Whether they hear or not, so long as they neither reason nor understand, they are equally deaf. Had He meant physical hearing, He would not have counted them the same as the deaf, nor closed the verse with reason. (And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind although they will not [attempt to] see (43) [Yunus] Had He meant physical sight, He would not have used the word "guide", for guidance is the very purpose of this sense; and how can anyone be guided without reasoning!? So He placed reasoning before guidance. For had he heard and reasoned, he would have seen with his heart and been guided, and that one sense would have spared him all the rest! (And We had certainly established them in such as We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and vision and hearts. But their hearing and vision and hearts availed them not from anything [of the punishment] when they were [continually] rejecting the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule (26) [Al-Ahqaf] And perhaps hearing lies closer to reasoning than sight does. An example of what we said earlier: Were someone to look at the planets (looking, a sense) and then think about them, his instinctive thinking would lead him to see that every effect has a cause (thinking); and that, in turn, would guide him to see that what is created has a Creator (reasoning, and then guidance). He arranged them in this order, thinking and then reasoning, in Surat Ar-Ra'd and Surat An-Nahl, because this is how human beings think: whatever the subject they ponder and work through, they move step by step from thinking to reasoning, which is straighter and fuller for them on the road to guidance. A person needs time when he thinks a matter through and takes it apart, before he arrives at mature and sound ideas; and quick, snap thinking is as far from reason as anything can be. Speed and haste in thinking, though a sign of intelligence, are also a cause of shallowness, especially with subjects we are tackling for the first time. So one should not rush ahead with a bold first idea before testing it and making sure of it. But with a subject he already knows, it is intelligent to think it through quickly. Guidance, then, is a method built on going step by step, on slowness in thinking and reasoning, not on speed and haste; for haste may lead a person astray and make him stumble. Another reason thinking comes before reasoning is that a person grows step by step from childhood to maturity, from instinctive thinking to reason; so this order fits better with the way he grows. Reason is a fruit, a coming of age; thinking is its cause; and the one may not be put before the other! Further evidence: with the Children of Israel, Allah the Exalted uses (Then will you not reason?), because they already held the proofs that Muhammad ﷺ was truly a prophet. They had no need of this gradual path; the knowledge had already come to them, and so they deserved rebuke and reproach. The evidence: (Do you order righteousness of the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason (44) [Al-Baqarah] (And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We have believed"; but when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has revealed to you so they can argue with you about it before your Lord?" Then will you not reason (76) [Al-Baqarah] (O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason (65) [Al Imran] And why, when He speaks of the signs of rain, does He use reasoning rather than thinking, as in Ar-Rum and Al-Ankabut? (And if you asked them, "Who sends down rain from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" they would surely say " Allah." Say, "Praise to Allah "; but most of them do not reason (63) [Al-Ankabut] (And of His signs is [that] He shows you the lightning [causing] fear and aspiration, and He sends down rain from the sky by which He brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason (24) [Ar-Rum] Because the Bedouin knows full well that it is Allah the Exalted who sends down the rain; he has no need of that first stage of thinking. So when he sees this sign, the rain falling and the earth brought to life after its death, the proof is already in his hands: will he not, then, reason and be guided to the Resurrection? Reflect with me: Allah argues with the People of the Book by their own scriptures, and with the polytheists by the signs of the heavens and the earth, and then says to each of them: the signs are clear and plain before you, and you have acknowledged them; so why will you not reason, and be guided!? And if you ask: Then why does He say to the Muslims (that you might give thought to this world and the Hereafter) Al-Baqarah, and (Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire (191) Al Imran I would answer that thinking and reasoning are found in all people, and that they had reached guidance and reasoned; yet in their faith in the signs of the heavens and the earth, and in the Quran, they too needed patience and unhurried care, a gradual passage from thinking to reasoning to guidance. And thinking is what carries a person from one station of faith to the next; If he thinks, then reasons, and arrives at a result close to the truth, he has reasoned; and if something better then becomes clear to him, he has thought, because he has gone back and thought again about the conclusion he reached. And so it is with every ascent in faith: each degree needs thinking, rethinking one's arrangements, one's life, one's values and character, and then reasoning and being guided to a better result than the one before. So one of the meanings of thinking is to question the earlier idea, the earlier method and the earlier result, and to take them apart again, in part or in whole, and reshape them until one is guided to something better. He may have a bad trait, such as stinginess, which he must pull down entirely and replace with generosity; and this, as you know, does not contradict the meaning of faith. Or he may be generous, yet need to refine what generosity means: not to squander, to keep his giving balanced, and to give everyone who has a right his due. (and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]") They thought, and so they reasoned that this creation is no idle play but has a wise purpose, and so they were guided to know that the Hereafter is true (then protect us from the punishment of the Fire). So they gave thought to this world and to the Hereafter. And from this we know that the believer never stops thinking; the cloak of silence does not suit him.

t: Subtleties and Fine Points of Hajj (Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Hajj Side by Side)
x: One of the wisdoms behind the rites Allah prescribed for Hajj is to remind us of the Day of Gathering. That is why He closed the verses on Hajj in Surat al-Baqarah with this very purpose: One of the wisdoms behind the rites Allah prescribed for Hajj is to remind us of the Day of Gathering. That is why He closed the verses on Hajj in Surat al-Baqarah with this very purpose: (And remember Allah during [specific] numbered days. Then whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays [until the third] - there is no sin upon him - for him who fears Allah. And fear Allah and know that unto Him you will be gathered) And with it He opens Surat al-Hajj! (O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the [final] Hour is a terrible thing (1) Al-Baqarah gives Hajj in brief; Surat al-Hajj gives it in full. So it dwells longer on the terrors of the Gathering (On the Day you see it every nursing mother will be distracted from that [child] she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people [appearing] intoxicated while they are not intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah is severe (2) [al-Hajj] And it sets out the rulings of Hajj in greater detail And it answers those who deny the Resurrection (O People, if you should be in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] indeed, We created you from dust..) Facing trials (And of the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss (11) [al-Hajj] And He gives an example of this turning back: When Satan cast rhymed words upon the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, Allah made that a trial to sift the believer from the hypocrite; and some did not hold firm, and went astray. (And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]. But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise (52) [That is] so He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those within whose hearts is disease and those hard of heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension (53) And so those who were given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and [therefore] believe in it, and their hearts humbly submit to it. And indeed is Allah the Guide of those who have believed to a straight path (54) [al-Hajj] He named the greatest cause of turning back on one’s heels: hypocrisy and hardness of heart; and in the verse that follows He named its cure: ikhbāt , humble submission, reverence, lowering oneself before Allah the Exalted (and their hearts humbly submit to it). And He unfolds it further here: (And for all religion We have appointed a rite [of sacrifice] that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. For your god is one God, so to Him submit. And, [O Muhammad], give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord] (34) Who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts are fearful, and [to] the patient over what has afflicted them, and the establishers of prayer and those who spend from what We have provided them (35) And the camels and cattle We have appointed for you as among the symbols of Allah; for you therein is good. So mention the name of Allah upon them when lined up [for sacrifice]; and when they are [lifeless] on their sides, then eat from them and feed the needy and the beggar. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful (36) [al-Hajj] In Surat al-Baqarah He forbade quarreling and wickedness in word and deed: insults, curses, abuse, foolishness, anger, and lust. Whoever strips himself of these traits will find the traits of ikhbāt from Surat al-Hajj settling in their place, for emptying comes before adorning: the trembling of the heart and its reverence when Allah is mentioned. That is why no one can be a quarreler without right, a habitual curser, and humbly reverent all at once! The two cannot meet. And whoever gives up wickedness and quarreling, Allah repays him with light in his heart “There is no gulp more beloved to Allah than a gulp of anger that a servant swallows; no servant swallows it for Allah’s sake but that Allah fills his inside with faith” And when you give up quarreling with your brother, He repays you with light in your heart and a door flung open to understanding, a fitting reward; for the clear opening belongs to the one who understands the clear Book, and this is won only through the toil of practice and clenched teeth. This is how I understand the hadith: whoever lets go of his anger, a door of understanding and wisdom is opened to him. (and [to] the patient over what has afflicted them): their patience, their refusal to turn back on their heels when trials and hardships strike them (And of the people is he who worships Allah on an edge..) (al-Hajj:11) And the establishers of prayer : everywhere else in the Quran it is wal-muqīmīna al-ṣalāh , except here in al-Hajj, where the nūn is dropped ( wal-muqīmī al-ṣalāh ); for the prayer is lightened for the pilgrim, who prays it combined and shortened —and Allah knows best—. He lightened the prayer for the pilgrim and pressed the giving upon him; that is why He said (those who spend from what We have provided them), keeping the nūn in yunfiqūn ; and the next verse makes clear what kind of spending is meant: the sacrificial offering of Hajj and the udhiyah. (And the camels and cattle We have appointed for you as among the symbols of Allah; for you therein is good. So mention the name of Allah upon them when lined up [for sacrifice]; and when they are [lifeless] on their sides, then eat from them and feed the needy and the beggar. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful (36) [al-Hajj] He knew that the one who gives up quarreling, absorbed in the Lord of Majesty and turned away from creation, does not keep watch over his enemies and what they weave behind his back. So He struck fear into those enemies, and reassured the humbly submissive that he should go on in his reverence and submission, and not break it off on their account, so great is the right of what he is engaged in, for Allah is enough for him. And so He said: (Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone treacherous and ungrateful (38) [al-Hajj] I reflected on Surat al-Baqarah and found that it begins with the verses of jihad and then Hajj, while Surat al-Hajj begins with Hajj and then jihad. Perhaps the wisdom is that, in Allah’s foreknowledge, they would fight (the battles of Badr ,,), then would come the Conquest and the Hajj, and then jihad once more. And how many a city did We destroy while it was committing wrong - so it is [now] fallen into ruin - and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace (45) So have they not traveled through the earth and have hearts by which to reason and ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts (46) There is a likeness between the land of the Gathering and the land of Hajj! Both stand bare of buildings (and you will see the earth prominent, and We will gather them): that is, bare and white, with nothing on it and no building, a level plain. So too the lands of the sacred sites, Arafah and Muzdalifah: no buildings stand on them. And He mentions the ruined towns so that the pilgrim remembers all he has left behind him, home, land, palaces, and family, and that he has come to perform the rites alone, solitary, stripped of everything, bare in an empty land: and so will you be on the Day of Resurrection. So too the Gathering comes after the terrors, after the splitting of the heavens, the constellations, and the moons; and so He mentions the ruined town, the abandoned well that no one draws from, and the lofty palace. Then He mentions traveling through the land, so that the pilgrim, as he moves from one sacred site to the next: Mina-Arafah-Muzdalifah- Mina, remembers that this is how all creation will be journeying to Allah on the Day of Gathering; so let him have a heart by which to reason.

t: Thank God I Am Not Famous
x: How often has fame left injustice in its wake: a person is drawn into some quarrel, and either he is wronged or he wrongs. How often has fame left injustice in its wake: a person is drawn into some quarrel, and either he is wronged or he wrongs. Or he rises to fame, is loved, gathers admirers across the earth, and then fame leaves him a single slip, filmed and passed from hand to hand; he is consumed with regret and sorrow, and cast aside the way carcasses are cast aside. And there is fame built on ignorance, so that all he does and says is ignorant; however many millions it brings in, it will soon wither away. Fame may come to someone through a scandal (we ask Allah the Exalted for well-being), so praise Him that He has covered us and kept us safe, hidden us from people's eyes, and drawn a veil over our faults. Soaring fame in his youth, the numbers, the money; then, in his mid-thirties, a thunderous fall: the world curses him and the numbers dwindle, he who was once the toast of everyone. And so his story is sealed with a death before death. Or perhaps his standing among people stayed high his whole life long, and only after death was he exposed and disgraced, so that his fame became a curse upon him. I ask Allah, for us and for you, a covering at death, after death and before death, and a sincere repentance before the chance is gone. And how often has soaring fame left behind regret, sorrow, crushing disappointment, and a gloom that imprisons a person until he cries out: "Oh, I wish that I were dust!" These are scenes that weigh upon the heart, I know. But I set them before you so that you may see how blessed you are, lose your appetite for the spotlight, and come to see obscurity as a great grace.

t: (And one who invites to Allah, by His permission, and an illuminating lamp)
x: You might describe a person as a moon; yes. You might describe a person as a moon; yes. You might describe them as a sun, or half a sun; yes. But to describe someone as both a sun and a moon? No! Never have the sun and the moon come together for anyone as they came together for Muhammad ﷺ (And the sun and the moon are joined). The moon is the Quran he brought, leading out of the darkness into the light. Whoever lives with the Quran alone is like one who lives beneath the full moon alone, never seeing the day; the affairs of this world and of faith are made whole only by the pure Prophetic Sunnah, just as the night is made whole by the day. The Quran is a night, and the Sunnah completes the whole of the day and the night. And the Quran is recited by night, is it not? The full moon never leaves the one who recites it, even while others wander blindly in the dark. And the Sunnah is the sun by which Allah completes and perfects the affairs of this world and of faith. Whoever holds to both has taken an abundant portion. (Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon) O Allah, send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.

t: How the Verses Hold Together
x: How the verses hold together: when He closed the verse on divorce with (And do not forget graciousness between you..), He was reminding us that the graciousness shown between people is not to be forgotten but kept alive by remembering it. Then He reminded us not to forget the right of the Creator, Glorified and Exalted is He, and to guard the prayers, for His is the greatest grace of all (Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer…), until He said (then remember Allah [in prayer], as He has taught you that which you did not [previously] know). How the verses hold together: when He closed the verse on divorce with (And do not forget graciousness between you..), He was reminding us that the graciousness shown between people is not to be forgotten but kept alive by remembering it. Then He reminded us not to forget the right of the Creator, Glorified and Exalted is He, and to guard the prayers, for His is the greatest grace of all (Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer…), until He said (then remember Allah [in prayer], as He has taught you that which you did not [previously] know). Another thread that binds the verses together: (Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses..), and among His verses is fighting in the cause of Allah: (Have you not considered those who left their homes in many thousands, fearing death?..), and right after it comes (And fight in the cause of Allah..). The two verses share one subject: urging jihad in the cause of Allah (under the banner of the ruler), and showing that fleeing from battle does not ward off death.

t: Whoever Knows Allah, What Does He Not Know?
x: "Whoever knows Allah, what is there left for him not to know? "Whoever knows Allah, what is there left for him not to know? And whoever does not know Allah, what is it that he knows?" To strike out across the earth, leaving behind the shelves of books and the clashing studies, to walk out of your library with your hair wild, seeking knowledge with your heart and carrying it to every heart: this, too, is a kind of knowing. Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you: some scholars said this means the piling up of books. "When you hear a hadith from me that your hearts recognize, that makes your hair and your skin grow soft, and that you feel to be near to you, then I am nearer to it than any of you. And when you hear a hadith from me that your hearts deny, that makes your hair and your skin shrink back, and that you feel to be far from you, then I am farther from it than any of you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew that hadiths would multiply and that knowledge would keep spreading and never shrink; so he made the heart's knowing one of the paths of learning. Faith itself is a kind of knowledge that people of reason acknowledge. And the heart's knowing is only as strong as faith and its branches, certainty and its shade, awe, reverent stillness, and humble lowliness before the truth and before people. Worship and faith are the water the heart drinks, and from it there springs up knowledge of what to say, what to do, and how to be.

t: (Indeed, Allah will be testing you with a river)
x: (He said, "Indeed, Allah will be testing you with a river") and they split into three groups: (He said, "Indeed, Allah will be testing you with a river") and they split into three groups: The disobedient: they scooped up more than one handful. Those who believed: they scooped up a single handful. The God-fearing: they did not drink at all. Disobedience screened the first group from even setting their hearts on obedience (obeying the king placed over them, and fighting alongside him in the cause of Allah); it sapped their resolve and drained their aspiration. And so this world teaches us that loving it is the lowest share of anything there is: whoever's aspiration stops at this point, you will find his strength feeble and his spirit defeated; he never learned that there are higher things, the highest of them al-Firdaws al-A'la, and above it the Throne of the Most Merciful. This is well known even in psychology: whoever sets himself a low goal comes to believe his abilities allow him no more than that, and walks away with poor, feeble results — what they call low competence. But whoever makes the Hereafter his concern — you will find his aspiration soaring high, like one who has stretched his abilities to their limit and given his horse free rein; he will not settle for the lesser and the lowly. He wants the highest in everything: in worship, in knowledge, in his specialty, in serving his country,,. And people will differ in their ranks in the Hereafter as their aspirations differed in seeking knowledge in this world; so look well at what you choose, and see clearly. The second group: those who believed with him; they scooped up a handful, taking what was permissible, yet the abundance of permissible things and distractions weighed them down from marching and fighting. The intention to fight did stir in them; they marched with him a little, and then they stopped (Then when he had crossed it along with those who believed with him, they said, "There is no power for us today against Goliath and his soldiers.") Patience whets the will for the long road, and he meant to keep them from the river not to punish them, but to test them and to train them in endurance. The third group: those who feared Allah and were patient -and can there be God-fearing without patience?- through thirst and fasting, through renunciation and scrupulousness, through drought and deprivation and want, through al-ba'sā' : poverty, and al-ḍarrā' : sickness. These are the ones who marched to the very end, and fought on with valor, with skill, and with humble pleading to Allah (they said, "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.") (But they drank from it, except a [very] few of them) and these few, who did not drink and held back out of scrupulousness, are the ones who said: (Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient.") Then look at His eloquent description of what lay behind their lofty aspiration, their steadfastness and their endurance: (those who were certain that they would meet Allah) Their aspirations were bound to the Hereafter; ( yaẓunnūn : yūqinūn , they were certain) of meeting Allah, and they chose what is better over what is lower, so they finished the march, and they persevered and were patient (So they defeated them by permission of Allah). The story tells us that whoever prefers the Hereafter to this world, his aspiration climbs and rises and towers like the mountains; that whoever triumphs over the whims and cravings of the self will endure and triumph in the battles of this world — and whoever has not triumphed here will not triumph there. True kingship is to be king over the kingdom of your own self. And whoever hopes for Allah and for meeting Him sees nothing of this world in front of him but he casts it aside, so nothing of this world will meet him except what he left behind him!, and what is behind him is behind him! Because the meaning is greater, the concern for the Hereafter weighs heavier, and Allah is more to be hoped for than any good or any hope. * And what is behind him is behind him!: meaning, what he put behind him he will find before him, and this is known in the Quran (Before him is Hell): warā'ihi ("behind him") means: before him.

t: (And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them)
x: (And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators) A parable Allah has struck for the one who was given the Quran and its clear proofs, yet did not act upon it. What made him swerve from guidance: following his desire in place of the Book, and preferring this world to the Hereafter. (And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators) A parable Allah has struck for the one who was given the Quran and its clear proofs, yet did not act upon it. What made him swerve from guidance: following his desire in place of the Book, and preferring this world to the Hereafter. But he detached himself from them: he cast off faith altogether, never to return. So Satan pursued him: this is as grave as it gets. The sinner follows Satan; but this man was a believing scholar who, after all his knowledge and faith, became a disbeliever, so Satan came after him and followed at his heels, and he became Satan's leader! And Satan his follower! See the eloquence of the parable; and all for the enormity of what he had done “The more abundant Allah the Exalted's blessings upon a person, the farther and greater his distance from Allah, should he turn away from Him; this is made plain by the words of Allah the Exalted: And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs …” al-Tafsir al-Muharrar. (And if We had willed, we could have elevated him thereby, but he adhered [instead] to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought) And if We had willed, we could have elevated him thereby, in this world and the Hereafter; but he sank down to (the earth: this world) and settled there (Ibn Kathir) So whether you rebuke him or leave him be, he is like the dog: pick up a stone and throw it at him, or leave him alone, and still he pants. And this man, whether you admonish him or not, never stops, never turns back from the misguidance he is in; he pants after this world, selling his soul to buy it. A lesson: the servant must do all he can to remain steadfast, by putting the Hereafter before this world, and choosing to follow the Quran over following his desire, so that Allah the Exalted may make him firm

t: Among the Truths of Spiritual Knowing
x: Among the truths of spiritual knowing: whatever fancies, schemes, and wishes you turn your mind away from come walking toward you in reality, easy and unforced —if Allah wills—. Among the truths of spiritual knowing: whatever fancies, schemes, and wishes you turn your mind away from come walking toward you in reality, easy and unforced —if Allah wills—. But if you arrange every last detail and forget the One who arranges all things, in whose hand are the decrees, to whom belong the reins of all affairs, and in whose hand are the keys; if you have reckoned with everything and counted every cost, then how is He to provide for you from where you do not expect!? Yes, we take the means; to neglect them is helplessness and sloth. But do not let your soul cling to these wishes too fiercely, for such clinging is a kind of craving and greed, and that does not become one who truly knows Allah. Have you not heard the words of the Exalted: (and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased)? He said tarḍāhā , “with which you will be pleased,” and not tahwāhā , “which you crave”; for his soul ﷺ was too perfect and too noble to hang upon a wish or a dream. And Moses (peace be upon him), when he counted out all that his staff could do: (He said, “It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses.”) ([Allah] said, “Throw it down, O Moses.”) He meant to teach him that the soul must not cling to any means, so He made the staff fearsome to him: (So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly). ([Allah] said, “Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.”) Now! Take it up by My leave and My will, not by your leave and your choosing! And once he had let it go and turned from it, Allah placed in it the miracle and the victory: it swallowed the sorcerers’ ropes, it split the sea, and through it they were granted victory even after his death. So whatever we let go of most completely, He has replaced with something better, beyond anything we could imagine. And when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, nurtures those who truly know Him, He raises them toward the most perfect of souls, through the purest letting go, and then being set free.

t: Be Kind to Your Children and Perfect Their Manners
x: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Be kind to your children, and perfect their manners.” From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Be kind to your children, and perfect their manners.” His words “Be kind to your children”: for kindness toward them only deepens their love for their parents. But because kindness may lead to bad manners, he pointed, with his words “and perfect their manners,” to the fact that kindness ought not to go that far.

t: The Righteous Dream
x: A righteous dream is a choosing from Allah the Exalted: He singles you out from among all His creation and lets you see it. A righteous dream is a choosing from Allah the Exalted: He singles you out from among all His creation and lets you see it. (And thus will your Lord choose you) Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Yaqub is telling his son Yusuf: just as your Lord has chosen you, and shown you these stars, with the sun and the moon, prostrating to you.." so too will He teach you the interpretation of dreams and complete His favor upon you by making you a messenger and sending revelation to you.

t: Ingratitude for a Blessing
x: It is ingratitude for a blessing to forbid it to yourself when Allah has made it lawful. It is ingratitude for a blessing to forbid it to yourself when Allah has made it lawful. Like someone who cuts out a whole kind of food, say dairy or bread, without any medical advice from a trustworthy, reputable doctor, and with no food allergy or anything of the sort; he is simply following the latest social media craze, with no logic and no reason behind it. Or like the one who banned eggplant, tomatoes, onions, watermelon and every fruit there is -except berries and cherries- and banned bread, rice, meat, poultry, eggs and dairy -a self-made doctor- Good grief, man, what have you left!? What do you actually eat? Food that does your body no harm, that you have no trouble with, when you are not on a diet and no doctor has told you to avoid it: why on earth do you forbid it!? Dr. Mustafa Abu Saad noted -in a podcast episode- that this generation faces three great phenomena and challenges in our time: 1- Atheism 2- sexual deviance 3- and eating disorders born of poor nutrition. That last problem, he says, comes from a generation of doctors that will arise forbidding everything! Don't eat this, or that, or the other, or, or,,, (Say, "Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision of which you have made [some] lawful and [some] unlawful?" Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?" And what will be the supposition of those who invent falsehood about Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful) Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And His saying: {Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people) …it may mean that He is full of bounty to the people in what He has made lawful for them of the good things He created in this world, and that He has forbidden them nothing except what harms them in their worldly life or their religion. (but most of them are not grateful) rather, they forbid what Allah has blessed them with, and they hem themselves in, making some things lawful and some unlawful." And Muhammad al-Maqdisi cited a statement of Taqi al-Din: "As for refraining from permissible things altogether, like one who refrains from eating meat, or eating bread, or drinking water … and thinks this is part of commendable asceticism, such a person is ignorant and astray — until he mentioned that Allah commanded eating of the good things, and giving thanks to Him" And the rule says: Whoever is harmed by honey, it is forbidden to him: that is, if honey harms this person's body, let him keep away from it until he recovers. But these people forbid with no harm, no logic, no reason and no justification! If only they forbade one thing or two; no, they forbid everything but a handful! Just like the people of the Jahiliyyah, who used to forbid kinds of food with no basis in revelation, reason, cause, medicine or harm — such as forbidding the slaughter and eating of a she-camel that had borne a string of females one after another, and forbidding milk to their women, and other strange things that we see today, only in a new and different guise, in the name of science and medicine!

t: Karāmah
x: Karāmah , the wonder granted to the righteous, is not that He folds up for you the distances of the earth, the lands in all their length and breadth. Karāmah , the wonder granted to the righteous, is not that He folds up for you the distances of the earth, the lands in all their length and breadth. No, karāmah is that He folds up for you the distance between the heart and the Lord: He lifts from it the veils that hold you back, cleanses it of the intoxication of union, clears away the barriers to understanding, erases the images the world has stamped upon you, and brings you better than them, or their like (Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent)? And He overpowers your wills with His will (and said to it and to the earth, “Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion.” They said, “We have come willingly”). He refers to the heaven with a pronoun of absence ( lahā , “to it”), and the meaning is that even the humblest of creations, the earth, obeyed; He mentions it to remind you! And at that, a person sees how small he is. So when the rescue of His gentleness reaches you, and the clouds of His mercy gather into view, His will overcomes your wills; and even if you do not want Him, He wants you (and because Allah guides whom He intends) O you, if this is not love, then what is?

t: At the Beginning of Your Relationship with the Quran
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: Listen to a surah you love, in the voice of a reciter you love — whether or not he has mastered tajweed, because the aim here is to build love between you and the Quran. At the beginning of your relationship with the Quran… Listen to a surah you love, in the voice of a reciter you love — whether or not he has mastered tajweed, because the aim here is to build love between you and the Quran. When a problem confronts you, or a thought nags at your mind and you want to be sure of it, open the Mushaf at random and see how it hands you the answer you need, whatever the problem — I know there is a juristic disagreement over this practice (seeking a good omen in the Quran), and I do not want to enter into it; but once again, the aim here is to forge a first bond with the Quran. Set yourself a portion of the Quran at the very start of your day, and never abandon it or put it off, whatever comes, for it is your impregnable fortress, the one you take with you to meet the toil and weariness of the day. Do not push it to the end of the day, after you have already taken so many blows! Prevention is better than cure, and this fortress gives you, by Allah's leave, strength, good hope, protection and care for the whole day; you feel companionship and richness filling your heart, and you feel that everything else the day brings, its provision and its people, is an extra, nothing more!

t: (Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He intends)
x: And, as its counterpart: (And thus have We sent the Qur'an down as verses of clear evidence and because Allah guides whom He intends) And, as its counterpart: (And thus have We sent the Qur'an down as verses of clear evidence and because Allah guides whom He intends) It is He who willed the entry into Paradise (Indeed, Allah does what He intends) And it is He who willed that the servant be guided in this world (and because Allah guides whom He intends). (And thus have We sent the Qur'an down as verses of clear evidence) Once the Quran had reached them, they parted into two groups: one that was not guided, so the Quran became a proof against them, for He did not will their guidance (Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts) And another for whom He willed guidance (and because Allah guides whom He intends) So whoever seeks guidance, let him take hold of the Quran Guidance He hastened to the believer in this world; Paradise He saved for him in the Hereafter It is He who willed the guidance, and He who willed the entry into Paradise. So no merit is yours, and no favour to boast of, in this or in that! "I love You with two loves: a love of passion, And a love because You are worthy of it. As for the love that is passion's love, It is my losing myself in Your remembrance, away from all but You. And as for the love of which You are worthy, It is Your drawing back the veils for me until I see You. No praise is mine in this, nor in that; Yours is the praise, in this and in that."

t: On the Meaning of the Quran Being a Mercy
x: I have always wondered: what does it mean that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, describes the Quran again and again as good tidings and mercy? Things are known by their opposites, and the opposite of mercy is torment. In more than one place, Allah the Exalted speaks of the inner torment and pain that befall those who do not follow al-Furqan , the Criterion, the Noble Quran. In Surah Al Imran He says: (And He revealed the Qur'an. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment). The exegetes explain that this severe punishment is the torment of the soul that makes the breast grow tight; that is why He called it severe: the torment of the soul, with all its anguish and pain. And in Surah Al-An'am: (So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to [contain] Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe). As for defilement ( al-rijs ): some said it is Satan, and this is the stronger view; others said al-rijs is torment, meaning the inner torment of one whose breast never opens, no matter what he does or achieves in this life: there is always that torment, that pain. But whoever follows guidance, believes, and holds fast to the Noble Quran, for him the Quran is what our Lord, Glorified and Exalted is He, said it is: a mercy for the believers, through which the believer is shown mercy. I have always wondered: what does it mean that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, describes the Quran again and again as good tidings and mercy? Things are known by their opposites, and the opposite of mercy is torment. In more than one place, Allah the Exalted speaks of the inner torment and pain that befall those who do not follow al-Furqan , the Criterion, the Noble Quran. In Surah Al Imran He says: (And He revealed the Qur'an. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment). The exegetes explain that this severe punishment is the torment of the soul that makes the breast grow tight; that is why He called it severe: the torment of the soul, with all its anguish and pain. And in Surah Al-An'am: (So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to [contain] Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe). As for defilement ( al-rijs ): some said it is Satan, and this is the stronger view; others said al-rijs is torment, meaning the inner torment of one whose breast never opens, no matter what he does or achieves in this life: there is always that torment, that pain. But whoever follows guidance, believes, and holds fast to the Noble Quran, for him the Quran is what our Lord, Glorified and Exalted is He, said it is: a mercy for the believers, through which the believer is shown mercy. Yes, I know there are people who turn to the Noble Quran to lift their worries, to ease their way, for provision and for knowledge, and that is good and well. The trouble is that it is a temporary goal. Once the goal of all that reading and all those completions is met (praise be to Allah, my debt was paid after I completed the Quran; praise be to Allah, I got the job after I completed the Quran), fine: then, once you have the job, do you abandon the Quran? Do you abandon the Quran? That is a short-term goal. And if the goal is not met, do you abandon the Quran? Do you abandon the Quran? I remember reading the story of a woman who used to complete the Quran again and again and join completion groups, and then she stopped: after three months she gave up completing it because the goal she wanted had not come true. Nothing happened, she said. That is the problem when we take up the Quran for aims and purposes other than the ones Allah the Exalted revealed it for. Allah the Exalted revealed the Quran as a mercy: so that peace, gladness, and richness of heart and spirit may come, so that they may blend together. It is also a blessing, a means of provision, and a means of multiplying good deeds, and with them, provision in this world. But the problem, as with this woman, was that through all those completions what she wanted never came, so she abandoned the Quran and abandoned the completions. Then she began to feel her heart tighten, and she said: I have lost something I had in the Quran, something that made me happy. And so she realized that its true purpose is happiness and peace, not provision alone, and she returned once more to completing it. If only the Noble Quran were taken as a cure for the soul and all it holds of desires, doubts, whims, emotions, and the rest; and taken, too, as a fortress for the soul and a source of its strength. This is what the daily portion of the Quran is for: every person must have a daily portion of the Quran, read or listened to in whatever voice he loves, never abandoned, never let go; and if he cannot manage a juz' of the Quran, then a single page a day. I remember one woman who had memorized the Quran telling me the story of how she did it. She said that at first she used to attend Quran classes, but then she spent a whole year reading one juz' every day. And she told me: Before that, I made sure to keep a daily portion of one page, and when I was under pressure, swamped with work and errands, then before I slept I would read even a single verse. And she told me: I really did do that, more than once; I was so pressed that day with work and errands that before I slept I opened the Mushaf, read one verse, closed it, prayed, and slept. So look how Allah the Exalted, when He saw her persevering and keeping up her reading, rewarded her by letting her memorize the Noble Quran; that was her reward. So let no one shortchange the Quran of its due. Let him begin his bond with it by listening or by reciting; he need not start at the beginning and go through to the end. He may read a particular surah he loves and repeat it. That is how the bond with the Quran begins: with something a person loves, so that afterward the Quran grows dearer and dearer to him. Now let us reflect on the last page of Surah Al-A'raf: (Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous). A few verses later, Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, says: (Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant). It is related that when Gabriel came down with this verse, the Messenger ﷺ said: I will turn away from the ignorant, but some resentment and anger toward him will still remain inside me. This is the meaning: take what is given freely, that is, take whatever people's characters allow; accept their manners as they are and do not ask for more; enjoin what is good, that is, what is right and known to be right; and turn away from the ignorant. Then the Messenger ﷺ said to Gabriel: But what of the anger, O Gabriel? And Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, revealed: (And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing). There are two views of this suggestion ( al-nazgh ). The first is that it is the urge toward a wrong: a person sets his mind on a sin, on disobedience; so when this suggestion, this urge, comes to him, let him seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan, the accursed. And according to most exegetes, al-nazgh here is also anger, so he seeks refuge in Allah the Exalted from it. Then He says: (Indeed, those who fear Allah - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him] and at once they have insight). The impulse ( ṭāʾif ) here, they said, is a passing thought, an evil thought: evil thoughts that come over a person. They remember: that is, they remember Allah the Exalted and remember the Home of the Hereafter, and seek refuge from Satan, the accursed, and the evil thought is gone. These are Satan's suggestions: hit him, curse her, do this; all of them are the whisperings of Satan, and their cure is seeking refuge and remembering: remembering the Hereafter, and being reminded by the Noble Quran, taking it up so that one holds back from anger, guards one's heart, and heals what is in it: the resentment smoldering in the breast, the anger, the rancor, and all the rest. Then He says: (But their brothers - the devils increase them in error; then they do not stop short). Their brothers are the human brothers of the devils: Satan comes to a person and whispers in his breast, do this, don't do that, and dresses it up for him, and he gives in and goes astray. Ibn Abbas said: Satan drives him toward sin, harrying him on; he goads him with desires and doubts, with whisperings, worries, and sorrows that goad him on and on into sin and disobedience: do this, say that, curse him, insult her; and so the breast is seething all the time. (In error; then they do not stop short): they increase them, that is, they keep feeding them such thoughts and notions. Then they do not stop short: they never let up, never weary of sin and disobedience, never weary, moving from one desire to the next, from one sin to the next, sinking ever deeper into error. That is the meaning. Then Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, gives the cure for the soul, for everything in the breast of resentment, anger, rancor, desire, and whim: (And when you, [O Muhammad], do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not contrived it?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This [Qur'an] is enlightenment from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.") And here is the heart of it: the cure through which a person is shown mercy is the Noble Quran, (that you may receive mercy). Allah the Exalted made it baṣāʾir , insights: (enlightenment from your Lord). Notice: not a single sight, but insights, as though one had more than one sight, more than one eye to see and behold with. And He made its purpose, and repeated it, that it bear the fruit of guidance and mercy: (and guidance and mercy for a people who believe). And then once more: (So when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy). Why? This mercy, the scholars said, is a mercy that reaches the believer in this world, and so does the guidance, just as with the patient: (Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided). They said: the blessings are the Lord's praise of them, and it comes in this world; and mercy and guidance come in this world too. And at the top of that same page He says: (Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous): whoever takes the Noble Quran to heart as his ally, Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, takes him as His ally, and by His mercy brings him in among the righteous, among His righteous servants and allies, who are shown mercy through this Book. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has His own people among mankind." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "The people of the Qur'an, the people of Allah and those who are closest to Him." In explaining this hadith, the scholars said: Allah the Exalted takes care of the people of the Quran as a guardian takes care of his household, or as a shepherd tends his own family; He watches over them in the affairs of this world and of the Hereafter, setting them right, guiding them, and making this Quran a mercy for them. Likewise in Surah Al-A'raf, the Exalted says: ([Allah] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses - Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet) to the end of the verse, where He says: (and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful). So He bound success and mercy together: He decreed this mercy for whoever follows the Book and the guidance, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Sunnah; and likewise success in this world and the Hereafter for whoever follows the Noble Quran and holds to it with strength. Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, also says in Surah Al-A'raf: (And there followed them successors who inherited the Scripture [while] taking the commodities of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it comes to them, they will [again] take it. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what was in it? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, so will you not use reason? But those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers). These were a later generation of the Jews who inherited the Scripture, taking the commodities of this lower life, that is, whatever of this world was put before them; they used the Scripture to grab at worldly gain, and lulled themselves with wishful thinking: It will be forgiven for us. And if an offer like it comes to them, they take it, taking what is forbidden; every aim of theirs was turned toward this world, and they were utterly, deeply heedless of the Hereafter. And this though they had studied the Scripture, memorized it, understood it, and read it; but they squandered it in practice, never living by it, as though they had never studied it at all. Then He mentions a second group, the opposite of the first: (But those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers). Some said this is a community among the Jews; others said it is the community that submitted and believed in Muhammad ﷺ; indeed, it is the nation of Muhammad ﷺ. (Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers): this shows that the Book guides a person, making him righteous in himself and then a reformer of others; and he cannot set others right before he has set himself right. So this Book sets a person right and brings him into righteousness.
