(Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous): by making him righteous in himself. (But those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers): by making him a reformer of others. Again and again, the Quran is spoken of as an inheritance: (Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants). And the Prophet ﷺ used a word drawn from the idea of succession: "I am leaving among you, that which if you hold fast to them," meaning the Book of Allah, the rope of Allah extended from the sky, "and my family - the people of my house," which is the Sunnah, "so look at how you deal with them after me ( takhlufūnī )." So the Quran is spoken of in terms of succession and inheritance; that is, Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, set the Quran and its worth on a par with an inheritance, as if a person had inherited a treasure, treasures upon treasures, riches; no, it is greater than any treasure. And succession ( khilāfah ) likewise: as if he possessed the earth. And as I see it, true kingship is for a person to possess himself, and the Noble Quran helps a person to master himself, his mind, and his desires. That is true kingship: to be king over yourself, ruler over yourself. That is true kingship. So part of the greatness of the Noble Quran is that it is described as an inheritance, a legacy, a heritage, and as succession.

t: The Wisdom of Forgetting
x: (We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget, except what Allah should will): proof that forgetting, and its opposite, remembering, lie within the will of Allah the Exalted and are part of His written decree. It also shows that forgetting is from Allah's decree, so whoever forgets should be content and not lose heart over it. (We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget, except what Allah should will): proof that forgetting, and its opposite, remembering, lie within the will of Allah the Exalted and are part of His written decree. It also shows that forgetting is from Allah's decree, so whoever forgets should be content and not lose heart over it. Forgetting happens for a great wisdom. Part of it is that Allah makes us forget our pain; for if we remembered it all, it would destroy us. Part of it, too, is that Allah may make us forget a certain piece of knowledge; for if we remembered it and passed it on to someone, it might lead them astray and into temptation rather than guide them! And the other way around: you may remember a piece of knowledge in front of one person and forget it in front of another, because it will help the one and harm the other. So He reminded you there, and made you forget here. In the hasan hadith: (My Lord, make me forget what You have decreed, and help me with what You have left me). The best way to deal with the past is to forget it, and if you cannot, then ask Allah for it! For none can make us forget but Allah the Exalted. And the best way to deal with the present is to turn toward what Allah the Exalted has given us. And Allah has wisdom and knowledge in making him forget what he meant to say. A person leans on Allah the Exalted in the most delicate workings of the mind, forgetting and remembering, and does not lean on the techniques and mechanisms of memory and the mind's forgetting alone. And part of the wisdom of forgetting is that Allah makes you forget a certain story; for had you told it before a certain gathering of people, you would have opened upon yourself a door of evil and strife that you knew nothing of, and that Allah knew. That is why He made you forget it. The wisdom of remembering: I asked Allah to make me forget the name of a poem so that I would stop searching for it, yet it kept echoing in my mind, and I wondered why. And the answer came: a test, a trial. And one should still take the means of remembering, such as digital tools, notes, and calendars, rather than trusting frail human memory, especially where people's rights and promises are concerned: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ feared he would forget something he needed, he would tie a thread around his little finger, or around his ring." Even though some have graded this hadith weak, its meaning is sound "Abdullah al-Lahji said: Forgetting, as some of the gnostics have said, belongs to the perfection of true knowing; for Allah the Exalted declared Himself free of it, and made it part of the very reality of the servant."

t: (Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward)
x: “Allah does not wrong a believer in a single good deed: he is rewarded for it with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for it in this world, so that when the Day of Resurrection comes, he has no good deed at all.” Sahih Muslim “Allah does not wrong a believer in a single good deed: he is rewarded for it with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for it in this world, so that when the Day of Resurrection comes, he has no good deed at all.” Sahih Muslim

t: (And their hearts absorbed [the worship of] the calf)
x: The love of the calf mingled with the very lining of their hearts, as water seeps into the depths of the body; and this because they denied the truth. The love of the calf mingled with the very lining of their hearts, as water seeps into the depths of the body; and this because they denied the truth. Ushribū (“they were made to drink”): as though someone else had made them drink the love of the calf, as though it had carried them to a point where they no longer had any choice. Here we learn that clinging to this world, and craving it, robs a person of freedom of spirit and of will: he becomes its slave, until it takes from him the most precious thing he owns, his freedom. The believer, you will find, is free, because he has broken loose from his desires and from his attachment to this world, and so he can say no to the forbidden; while the one without faith, whom the world has mastered, says yes to everything in it, out of his attachment to it and his bondage to doubts and forbidden desires. There is an eloquent image here, too: their hearts soaked up their love of the world the way the earth soaks up water. Their life and their nourishment came from it, so that their deeds and their disobedience became the fruit of the very water they had been made to drink. We hold fast to Allah, and seek refuge in Him from such a state. It also shows that sin left unrepented leads to love of this world and all it holds, to clinging to it and craving it. (al-Tafsir al-Muharrar)

t: The Chosen Message on the Path of Being Chosen (Reflections on the Verses of Al-Imran)
x: When the prophet informed the Children of Israel that Talut had been sent to them as king, they said in astonishment: how can he have kingship when he is poor, with neither lineage nor wealth, while we are the ones descended from the line of kings!? So he informed them that his qualifications for being chosen were "knowledge and ability" (and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature). He mentioned knowledge first because of its great honor, and stature is the strength that qualifies him for war; it is any ability and talent with which Allah has blessed a person. Qualifications for Being Chosen When the prophet informed the Children of Israel that Talut had been sent to them as king, they said in astonishment: how can he have kingship when he is poor, with neither lineage nor wealth, while we are the ones descended from the line of kings!? So he informed them that his qualifications for being chosen were "knowledge and ability" (and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature). He mentioned knowledge first because of its great honor, and stature is the strength that qualifies him for war; it is any ability and talent with which Allah has blessed a person. But here we are not talking about kingship; rather, about Allah's choosing of His righteous servants to bring them near to Him in the stations of servitude. When Allah chooses a servant, He doesn't ask him for 10 years of experience! Nor for passion and desire, not at all! Even if he were drowning in darkness, the will of Allah is above the will of every creature, even if he resists guidance and hates it. But there are qualities observed in those whom Allah chooses: Humility: toward the truth and surrender to it; because Allah does not guide an arrogant one (I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right). Supplicating for guidance: that He make him righteous and admit him among the righteous Love of knowledge, searching for the truth, diligence and hard work; and any knowledge at all! For Allah loves resolve and taking the books with strength, and this qualifies him tomorrow to study His Mighty Book. Ability and talent in anything: so that tomorrow he becomes a hope that strengthens his society and the homeland he lives in, if he becomes righteous and then a reformer. The Surah of the Righteous (Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.") The path of love is in these two: Quran and Sunnah; whoever follows them and acts upon them, his face has succeeded. Then He mentioned that the path to the love of Allah has landmarks and stars, in whose footsteps a person walks and so reaches it: (Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran over the worlds. Descendants, some of them from others. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.) I reflected on it: He mentioned Adam and Noah singly, but as for Abraham He mentioned his household, and likewise the family of 'Imran; because their descendants were righteous, so they were a house radiating light. So the surah set out in it the conduct and path of the awliya, to follow their example on the path of righteousness and wilayah, and that is why He named it Al-Imran; and because of the standing of Abraham (peace be upon him), He mentioned him often in this surah. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing: "And Allah knows who deserves to be chosen, so He chooses him; for He hears their words, and knows their states and what is in their consciences; that is why He favored them and chose them..in it is an indication that He chose them with complete knowledge of them; as an encouragement toward their states and toward following their deeds and words ." al-Tafsir al-Muharrar (and of the righteous) an explanation that there is no rank greater than a person being righteous; because in all actions and abstentions he persists upon the most righteous way and the most complete path, and it is known that this encompasses all stations in worldly life and in religion, in the actions of the hearts and in the actions of the limbs" al-Tafsir al-Muharrar The beginning of the path is guidance and the second part is good tidings (guidance and good tidings) Then, if one's foot becomes firm in guidance, the good tidings come to him in the middle! (So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings") by way of hastening openings for the one who hastens to good deeds And the foot does not become firm except through knowledge (And those firm in knowledge) “Whoever fulfills his oath, whose tongue is truthful, whose heart is upright, and who keeps his stomach and private parts chaste; that is the one firm in knowledge” And al-Fakhr said: he is the one who knows Allah, and the one who knows the Quran. And the summary: being firm in knowledge is not through the abundance of books and memorized texts, but through acting upon the Quran and studying it, knowing Allah, and earnest striving with action and knowledge on this path. Uprightness of heart! (O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds) The ranks of being chosen: 1- Being chosen over the self: by purification from faults and sins (indeed Allah has chosen you) 2- Being chosen over the group: (and chosen you above the women of the worlds). "He chose her for her abundant worship, her asceticism, her nobility, and her purity from impurities and whisperings" — Ibn Kathir And likewise John (peace be upon him) (a leader and ḥaṣūran (“abstaining”)) ḥaṣūran , meaning withholding himself from desires, and he attained this station through much striving. And whoever neglects striving will have much torment of the soul! -for you are free, and your choice is the pain or the cure- (Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment) :in it is a likening of what befalls the soul of the narrowness and pain of punishment, to one who is bound tight, fettered, and constricted" .-al-Tafsir al-Muharrar And the one who devotes himself to the Quran, acting upon it, reciting it; is in healing and a garden (Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire) He beautified them in the soul; as a test, and were it not for them, the hypocrite would not be distinguished from the believer, nor the believer from the God-fearing, nor the God-fearing from the pure one who puts nothing before the love of Allah And in al-Bukhari, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: (O Allah, we cannot but rejoice at what You have made beautiful for us. O Allah, I ask You that I spend it in its right way). And the meaning of Allah's beautifying is: by bringing into existence and making ready for benefit, and creating the natural disposition to incline toward these things. And Allah the Exalted beautifies them as a trial and a test; because were it not for the beautifying of these things in people's hearts, the true believer would not be known. For the one strong in faith does not put them before the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." al-Tafsir al-Muharrar Guarding the frontiers of the soul is the greatest ribat: guarding against thoughts and memories, lest their scent and stirring slip through to the heart, and turning them away with seeking refuge and saying la ilaha illa Allah And He concluded Al-Imran with this meaning (O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful) Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) mentioned the reason this verse was revealed: "There was no battle in the time of the Prophet ﷺ in which they would remain stationed; rather, it was revealed about people who frequent the mosques, praying the prayers at their times, then remembering Allah in them. (Persevere) in the five prayers, (and endure) against yourselves and your desires, (and remain stationed) in your mosques." — Ibn Kathir “Performing ablution thoroughly despite difficulties, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer; that is the ribat …and he repeated it three times” Whether you show what is within yourselves..: "a direction toward purifying the hearts and being mindful of Allah's knowledge at all times, so that the servant is ashamed before his Lord that He should see his heart as a place for every bad thought; rather, he occupies his thoughts with what brings him near to Allah…what is in your breasts: the inner selves and consciences, and this follows the known usage of the language of attributing the soul's thoughts to the breast and the heart; because the emotions of the soul and the hesitations of thinking are all felt as movements in the breasts " al-Tafsir al-Muharrar (And caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah) Mary (peace be upon her) was in the care of Zechariah, and this is Allah's good raising of her: that He placed before her a role model whom she would follow in righteous deeds. So whoever wants the path of guidance; let him watch the righteous, mix with them, attach himself to them, search for them, listen and read, so that perhaps a spark of blessing reaches him. The Blessings of Withholding (Never will you attain the good [reward] until you spend [in the way of Allah] from that which you love) and after it came (All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had made unlawful to himself) (Israel: Jacob) made camel meat unlawful to himself because of the sciatica he had. The connection between the two verses: You will not attain any good, including the path of guidance, except through two things: 1- That you spend some of what you love (He said: from that which you love, and this is from His mercy to us, meaning some of it, not all of it) and He did not restrict it: spending is general and includes everything Allah has provided you: time, knowledge, wealth,, So you will not attain the knowledge of the Quran and its understanding, and reach the peak of action and its reality, until you give it all your time so that it gives you some of itself 2- Deprivation: that you deprive yourself of what you love, crave, and desire. And among these are whims: you keep yourself from them and besiege them (and ḥaṣūran ), as though he lays siege to desires, so when the winds of withholding arrive, the gusts of gifts come, and this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Ata'illah (the withholding was the very essence of the giving). (So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes) The emigration of the awliya is emigration from evil: evil deeds, evil companions, and everything unbefitting people of honor. “The emigrant is the one who abandons evil” “The emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden” These are the ones whose supplication Allah answered (Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers..) they sought victory hastily in this world, so He informed them of the answer to their supplication (And their Lord responded to them..) because of their emigration, their patience, and their striving. (Distinguished in this world and the Hereafter) Distinction in this world: through Sharia knowledge. Al-Shafi'i said: "Allah has never taken an ignorant person as a wali; if He takes him, He teaches him". That is because worship alone without knowledge may make the feet sink instead of making them firm, and Satan makes it seem fair to the one who does it, and perhaps he falls into extremism and other afflictions. So the wali must have beneficial knowledge that he learns and teaches, and righteous deeds that bring him near. He found with her provision: books and pages of knowledge. For knowledge is the provision of the one who knows Allah, and his sustenance. (They are not [all] the same; among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in obedience], reciting the verses of Allah during periods of the night and prostrating [in prayer]) They are the community from the People of the Scripture who entered Islam; so they stood in prayer at night while people slept. And we cannot imagine a wali of Allah who does not pray the night prayer or witr, even if just one rak'ah, and we cannot imagine a wali of Allah who has no daily portion of the Quran, even if just one verse. Gifts of Love and Grants of Nearness He concluded this path by showing that whoever is patient on the path of wilayah attains it by the enabling of Allah (whoever walks the path arrives) ✨ And there came to him all kinds of honors, the sweetness of openings, and victory over enemies "that patience and God-fearing repel enemies; because of His saying, Glorified is He: And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all" al-Tafsir al-Muharrar And victory in this world and the Hereafter (and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection) they are the nation of Muhammad ﷺ, who follow all the messengers, and by this Allah honors them with victory in this world and the Hereafter But as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards ( that is: as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will complete for them their recompense of reward without decrease or deprivation, in this world and the Hereafter; in this world through victory and triumph, honor, a good life, a good name, and other than that, and in the Hereafter through Paradise and lasting bliss " al-Tafsir al-Muharrar

t: Lessons of Defeat and Brokenness (Reflections on the Verses of Al Imran 2)
x: (Here you are loving them but they are not loving you) (Here you are loving them but they are not loving you) Allah marvels at the believers’ love for the hypocrites! And all the while the hypocrites hate them! “In it is a marvel at the two states taken together: the wonder is that the believers love them while they hate the believers.” So do not give your love to one who hates you. (And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you ..) He promised you victory at Uhud, but the promise was bound to obedience; when you disobeyed, there came the breaking and the defeat. Victory comes only through obedience. No victory lasts forever! Victory at the start of the battle, then pride, then the fall A great victory turns into a crushing defeat the moment disobedience creeps in (Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you, while another faction worried about themselves) Even in defeat and calamity, the believer holds a wondrous calm, while the hypocrite is consumed by worry for himself: terror keeps him from sleep What do you do after a battle you have lost? You go on —with the blessing of Allah— to the next battle (Those [believers] who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them) Despite the wounds they had taken at Uhud, as they were making their way back to Medina, the Messenger ﷺ ordered them out to Hamra al-Asad, and they answered and obeyed. The Battle of Uhud: on a Saturday And Hamra al-Asad: on the Sunday, in Shawwal Not “I’ll come back tomorrow,” or “in four months,” “Let me learn my lessons first!” No! That is not how failure is met. Learning from failure happens in the moment: now, as it strikes, and then you march to battle the very next day. One night to take in the lessons, to analyze and reflect, and tomorrow morning you put them into practice The illusion of the enemy: the illusion of their power and might. This is Satan’s work: he whispers into your chest to frighten you and sap your resolve, and then, when you meet them, you find them to be nothing, so long as you are God-fearing and a believer (That is only Satan who frightens [you] of his supporters. So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are [indeed] believers) “So if he tempts you and fills you with illusions, rely on Me and take refuge in Me, for I am sufficient for you and will give you victory over them” - Ibn Kathir And there is nothing better than to say: Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.

t: (And Whatever Good You Do – Allah Knows It)
x: (And whatever good you do – Allah knows it): why did He hold back the word (or evil?) (And whatever good you do – Allah knows it): why did He hold back the word (or evil?) "When I know good of you, I mention it and make it known; and when I know evil of you, I veil it and hide it — so that you may know: if this is how My mercy treats you in this world, then what will it be in the Hereafter?" "The second: some of the exegetes said, explaining His words ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming – I almost conceal it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 15], that it means: had it been possible for Me to conceal it even from Myself, I would have done so. So too with this verse. It is as though the servant were told: whatever good you do, I know it; but the evil you do — had it been possible for Me to conceal it even from Myself, I would have done so." - al-Razi O Allah, forgive us what they do not know of us, and make us better than they think us to be. I seek the forgiveness of Allah, the Almighty, and I turn to Him in repentance.

t: (Satan Threatens You with Poverty) Then (He Gives Wisdom to Whom He Wills)
x: (Satan threatens you with poverty …) and right after it comes (He gives wisdom to whom He wills..) (Satan threatens you with poverty …) and right after it comes (He gives wisdom to whom He wills..) Wisdom: the Quran, and the scholars agreed that what is meant by it here is understanding the Quran — its abrogating and abrogated verses, and its meanings. And what my own reflection has led me to is this: the Quran — recited, memorized and understood, and above all read and heard explained in its exegesis — shields a person from the whispers of Satan, the whims of the self, and immorality in all its forms: stinginess, greed, insults, cursing and the like. So whoever wants guidance, and wants to reach the very summit of happiness, let him hold fast to the Quran: set aside a daily portion and never abandon it, then look at the richness in your heart, and how it turns away from desires and sins. Fortify your heart with it at the start of the day, not at its end.

t: After the Verses of Victory, Allah Speaks of Wealth!
x: In Al-Baqarah: (Or do you think that you will enter Paradise…. until [even their] messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near) and then comes (They ask you, [O Muhammad], what they should spend..) In Al-Baqarah: (Or do you think that you will enter Paradise…. until [even their] messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near) and then comes (They ask you, [O Muhammad], what they should spend..) When He willed to affirm that victory would come without fail — while minds had come to doubt it, so long had it tarried — He set down, to seal that certainty and banish every doubt, the rulings on spending the spoils! As if to say: you will be granted victory, without fail and beyond doubt; but that is not what matters. What matters more is this: what will you do, after victory, with the wealth and provision that come your way? Be mindful of Allah in it, and spend it as He has ordained. In Al Imran: He mentions the Battle of Badr (And already had Allah given you victory at [the battle of] Badr while you were few in number. Then fear Allah; perhaps you will be grateful), then He mentions the prohibition of consuming usury (O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied..) Fear Allah regarding the victory He gave you, and thank Him by leaving off sin: do not consume usury and slide into arrogance and insolence. Indeed, victory is one of the moments for seeking forgiveness, for whoever is granted a conquest. Allah commanded the Children of Israel, when they entered (the city: Jerusalem), to say ḥiṭṭah , meaning "O Allah, take our sins away from us"; but they went in saying ḥinṭah (wheat). They did not give thanks; they disobeyed (And [recall] when We said, "Enter this city… and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens' [ ḥiṭṭah ]") And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Makkah in conquest with his head bowed, reciting the verses of his Lord and seeking forgiveness (When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance) Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.

t: The Art of Untying Psychological Knots (as in the Quran)
x: In Makkah they cursed them and tormented them, until the very sight of the Kaaba came to hurt the Muslims! How could we perform Hajj and ʿUmrah, aching as we look upon the places of torture and the corners of cruelty!? And when Allah knew what lay in their souls, He said to them: The First Scene: In Makkah In Makkah they cursed them and tormented them, until the very sight of the Kaaba came to hurt the Muslims! How could we perform Hajj and ʿUmrah, aching as we look upon the places of torture and the corners of cruelty!? And when Allah knew what lay in their souls, He said to them: (And complete the Hajj and 'umrah for Allah) You do not perform Hajj for the sake of people, nor for those of the days of ignorance, nor for the idols you see, nor for the insults that wounded you... no, you perform Hajj for the sake of Allah the Exalted. He untied every one of their psychological knots and emotional associations with a single password: Tawhid: devoting your aim, in all that you do, purely to Allah alone, not to those pains, and not to those memories The word (Allah) alone wipes everything away, and after it everything is bathed in light. And when the thing you strive for is good, yet hedged about with what is hateful and hard, the hardship should not turn you away from it. For what is good is worth bearing, hardships and all, so long as the intention is for Allah. Ibn Ashur said: "And they are the ones who barred the Muslims from it; [the verse came] lest the Muslims grow weary of the Hajj in which they had suffered the harm of the polytheists. So they were told: that must not keep you from desiring Hajj and ʿUmrah, for you perform Hajj for Allah alone, not for the sake of the polytheists; and because when something good and desirable is hedged about with what is hateful, that should not turn one away from it; rather, that obstacle must be removed from it, and one of the ways of removing it is the fighting alluded to in the preceding verses. It may also be that the qualification in His words (for Allah) serves to purify the intention of what used to cloud people's intentions in the days of ignorance: seeking nearness to the idols" The Second Scene: In Madinah And when the Muslims had been defeated at Uhud, and they passed by the mountain, the Prophet ﷺ said: Uhud, we love it and it loves us! He did not say it as a mere historical remark; he said it to heal the associations that had formed in their souls, or to keep them from ever forming in the generations to come. The lesson here: using spoken words to untie knots and associations (any phrase that is helpful and meaningful) So the one who fell over in the ice cream shop while the customers laughed at him should go back to that shop (the courage to face down imagined fears and inner dread), and then say to himself, out loud: Falling the first time doesn't mean you'll fall the second time! It's fine, try again What, do these new customers know you and know what happened? Come off it, Mr. World-Famous! And other cheerful words like these, until your heart grows strong. And likewise, devoting your intention and aim purely to Allah the Exalted; for it is among the greatest means of untying the soul's associations.

t: (And of the people is he who sells himself, seeking means to the approval of Allah. And Allah is kind to [His] servants)
x: The believer in this world is like the mukātab slave (and we are all slaves of Allah): a slave whose master has agreed with him on a fixed sum of money, and the moment he pays it in full, his master sets him free. The believer in this world is like the mukātab slave (and we are all slaves of Allah): a slave whose master has agreed with him on a fixed sum of money, and the moment he pays it in full, his master sets him free. So the believer buys himself back, ransoming his soul from doubts, whims and cravings, until not a single debt remains on him, not even an atom's weight of whim, without his having freed himself from it. And the deeper he goes into bondage to Allah the Exalted, the more he is freed from bondage to everything else: the world and all its creatures. The more complete the servitude, the more beautiful and the sweeter the freedom.. That is true freedom: freedom of the spirit, not of wealth or body or self. A freedom in which a person truly, genuinely chooses what he loves and what he hates; a freedom that cares nothing for people's blame or praise; a freedom that began with the Truth and ends in Him, far removed from creation; a freedom stripped of the garments of fame, praise and blame, of hatred and love. Something from above. And how could what is from above descend, to be grasped by lowly minds that cling to the world, whose souls are bound up in it? "So when he abandons disbelief and sin and steps forward into faith and obedience, it is as though he has bought himself free of the punishment and the Fire. The believer, then, is like the mukātab , who pays a counted number of dirhams and buys himself with them; so too the believer spends a counted number of breaths and with them buys himself forever. But the mukātab remains a slave as long as a single dirham is still owed; and likewise the one under obligation is never released from the bondage of servitude as long as he has a single breath left in this world." al-Razi He closed the verse with kindness to affirm that whoever bears these traits (selling himself, seeking the approval of Allah) will receive Allah's good gifts and His mercies, in this world and the Hereafter "Kindness here stands, by metonymy, for what it entails, namely the bestowal of good things, just as mercy does And the apparent sense is that the definite article in His words al-ʿibād (“the servants”) is one of totality, for Allah is kind to all His servants, though they differ in their share of it: among them are those whom Allah's kindness reaches in this world and in the Hereafter, in differing measures in each, as Allah's knowledge and wisdom decree" Ibn Ashur

t: Encouraging the Self
x: Encouraging the self: it appears in His words (And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking means to the approval of Allah and assuring [reward for] themselves) Encouraging the self: it appears in His words (And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking means to the approval of Allah and assuring [reward for] themselves) Tathbīt al-nafs , making the self firm: encouraging it to give, and strengthening it. And I leave you to dwell with the words of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him: (This is the parable of one whose spending springs from sincerity and truthfulness: seeking His pleasure, glory be to Him, is sincerity, and making firm from within is truthfulness in giving. For whoever spends meets two banes as he spends; if he escapes them both, his likeness is the one mentioned in this verse: The first: that he seeks by his spending praise or acclaim, or some worldly aim of his, and this is the state of most who spend. The second bane: the weakness of his soul in giving, its holding back and its wavering: should he do it or not? The first bane is removed by seeking the pleasure of Allah, and the second bane is removed by making firm; for making the soul firm means encouraging it, strengthening it, and urging it forward to give) Righteous deeds, too, have inner motives, all turned toward a single aim: Allah the Exalted. And a person nurtures his own inner motives, and encourages himself by himself "The merit of spending out of firmness from within oneself: such spending is driven by an inner motive, not by someone else's urging or advice, as the Exalted says: wa tathbītan min anfusihim (and assuring [reward for] themselves)" al-Tafsir al-Muharrar And that he gives with a generous soul and a love of giving, not grudgingly; for the hypocrite's motives rest on others ( istawqada nāran , “kindled a fire”: the hypocrite relies on others in his faith and his deeds, which is why He said istawqada , “sought to kindle,” and not awqada , “kindled”; for he looks to others to help him kindle his faith) (and that they do not spend except while they are unwilling)

t: Our Lord, Give Us in This World [That Which Is] Good and in the Hereafter [That Which Is] Good
x: And among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have in the Hereafter no share: this is a warning to the believer not to be like the disbeliever, who asks for nothing but this world and has no faith in the Hereafter. And among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have in the Hereafter no share: this is a warning to the believer not to be like the disbeliever, who asks for nothing but this world and has no faith in the Hereafter. Instead, ask Allah for the good of this world and of the Hereafter: (But among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.") Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account: that is, the believers who pray for the good of this world and the Hereafter will have their prayers answered: He gives them (a share: a portion), whether small or great, of what they have earned, meaning of what they prayed for. And Allah is swift in account: He hastens to answer your prayers, a reward for those who believed in the Hereafter and did not settle for this world alone. "For if you ask Him, He will give you a share of what you asked for, in this world and in the Hereafter; and Allah hastens to answer your prayers." Ibn Ashur

t: Among the Meanings of Patience: Fasting
x: Among the meanings of patience: fasting! Among the meanings of patience: fasting! {O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer} Patience here is fasting, and prayer holds the Quran within it. That is: seek help, in the affairs of this world and the next, through fasting, the Quran, and prayer. “By patience He meant fasting. Imam Ahmad said: We have narrated this from Mujahid. This is because fasting holds patience within it: holding back by day from the food and drink one is used to, while one’s nature stirs toward them and the soul longs for them. And this is why Ramadan was called the month of patience.” “Abu Ubayd said: It reached me that Sufyan ibn Uyaynah explained His words as referring to fasting. He said: Because fasting is patience; a person holds himself back from food, drink, and intimacy. Then he recited: {Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account}” (Shu‘ab al-Iman) Fasting is a brightness that burns away sins and cravings; the flash of its lightning all but takes away the sight! It grants a wondrous keenness of insight, and a strength of perception and knowledge; for the Prophet ﷺ said: “and prayer is a light, … and endurance is a brightness” That is: fasting is a brightness. Al-Bayhaqi took this hadith as proof that one of the names of fasting is patience. And al-Asqalani said in al-Fath : “‘…fasting; it is for Me, and I shall reward for it’: that is, I shall reward it with a great reward, without fixing its measure. This is like the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾. End of quote. And the patient are those who fast, according to most views… I say: Abu Ubayd preceded him in this, in his Gharib , saying: It reached me that Ibn Uyaynah said that, and he argued for it on the grounds that fasting is patience, because the one fasting holds his soul back from its desires, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾” Fasting is a cure for the heart And the proof, backed by the authentic hadith: “Whoever would be glad to have much of the rancor in his chest taken away, let him fast the month of patience and three days of every month,” And in another wording: “Fasting three days of the month takes away the rancor of the chest” “He says: ‘Among the things that take away much of the rancor of the chest,’ that is, that remove from it deceit and malice, or its seething anger, or its hypocrisy, or the fiercest wrath, ‘is fasting the month of patience,’ which is Ramadan, ‘and fasting three days of every month’: so after Ramadan it suffices to fast three days of every month throughout the year, and this equals fasting the whole year, since every good deed is worth ten like it; a month is worth ten months, and three days of every month equal the whole month.” - al-Durar al-Saniyyah (dorar.net) The benefit of fasting is reaped through repetition; as al-Asqalani pointed out regarding the hadith “O young people! … should fast,” what is meant is fasting again and again. That is what bears the fruit and sharpens insight

t: Guidance and Good Tidings

t: Untying Emotional Associations and Ties to the Past
x: A task I always hand my mind: untying emotional associations and ties to the past! A task I always hand my mind: untying emotional associations and ties to the past! Say something embarrassing once happened to you in an ice cream shop. Now, every time you see its logo and its colors, the moment comes rushing back, and you feel miserable and mortified You could treat it as a mental puzzle and hand it to your mind to untangle: untie that link, please! Ignore it, forget it, nobody even noticed you, and honestly, nobody is souring their own mood over it but you! And what actually happens? You walk into that shop happy, and you enjoy yourself. Who ties the knots and forges the links? You. Who unties them? You. And beware of excessive, overwrought emotional expression, for it is among the greatest causes of misery! It only makes the associations stronger and sharper Keep to moderation in what you feel: anger, embarrassment, love, joy, and sorrow. Do you see now why his laughter ﷺ was a smile? And do you know why he forbade tearing at one's clothes and striking one's face in grief? Because exaggerated emotional expression wrecks the mind and the spirit. And keep away from every source that feeds you exaggerated expression: certain posts, the news, videos, stories,,, Even in your body language, avoid overexpression. Some people find, in every corner of life, a reminder of misery and resentment; and some find, in every atom of it, a reminder of gratitude and contentment.

t: The Times When Worship Is Forbidden
x: The times when worship is forbidden are the examinations of the devoted and the trials of those who love: will they have the patience to put off their worship until the hour has passed? The times when worship is forbidden are the examinations of the devoted and the trials of those who love: will they have the patience to put off their worship until the hour has passed? And if we told you the marvels of those people of old, you would be astonished! They told us of a young man so in love with fasting that he could not bear the days of Tashreeq, and he went hunting for legal loopholes, some clever way to find himself an excuse to fast! Until he feared disobeying the Messenger ﷺ — and so he held back, and obeyed. And Ali ibn Bakkar said: For forty years nothing has grieved me but the breaking of the dawn. I say: perhaps what grieved him was the hour of being held back; then, when the sun had risen, he would pray, and the intimacy would return. And women in their time of menstruation, and the tightness they feel: she finds no rest until she returns to prayer, and if it comes upon her in the last ten nights or on the Day of Arafah, that is a great trial from her Lord. Yet if she is patient and bears being kept from fasting and prayer, and takes up remembrance, the Quran and supplication, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good. And no place is harder on one who remembers Allah than the lavatory, where his tongue, once flowing freely, is held back from remembrance — so much so that Ibn Baz used to wrap his turban over his mouth when he entered the lavatory! And perhaps this is among the wisdoms of saying Ghufrānaka ("Grant me Thy forgiveness"): with it he soothes his longing! And so, whoever holds himself back from sin, Allah repays him by holding him back from worship — out of longing and love! And whoever is patient against the self's seductions toward sin, Allah exchanges them for its seductions toward obedience!

(and spend out of what We have provided for them): this covers every kind of provision, knowledge, wealth, and children, as al-Fakhr said. “There is to be no envy except for two: A man to whom Allah grants wealth and he spends from it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day. t: A Love Ruled by Reason
x: When a soul reaches its perfection, its love for things and for people becomes pure of whims and free of mere emotion. When a soul reaches its perfection, its love for things and for people becomes pure of whims and free of mere emotion. You love them because you want guidance and good to reach them; this is a love born of reason, not of what you stand to gain from them, nor of their beauty, their looks, their coloring or their voices. So sincerity of purpose, even in how you deal with people, is the perfection of the soul and of love. And so it is with goals and ambitions in life {We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased} He said tarḍāhā , “with which you will be pleased,” and not tahwāhā , “which you crave,” or tuḥibbuhā , “which you love,” because the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was perfect. He loved that the qiblah should face the Kaaba because it was built on the oneness of Allah and so has the greater claim, not because it was his homeland, nor out of loyalty to his tribe. Such was the perfection of the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: his heart did not cling to any particular thing; whatever he wanted in his heart, he wanted for the sake of good. Tarḍāhā : “And since being pleased conveys a love that arises from reasoning, it was chosen in this context rather than tuḥibbuhā or tahwāhā ” (Ibn Ashur) So the love that rests on reasons of the mind and of faith is the most perfect love. Strive with your soul until it loves this way, then look at the blissful ease you find yourself in. “I love humanity, but I wonder at myself. The more I love humanity in general, the less I love man in particular.” It seems Dostoevsky had reached a high degree of maturity, so high that he had freed himself from bearing any one individual a special love and a particular affection, and had begun to grasp that there is a general love for all human beings. As for our special, wholehearted love, it belongs to a Being higher than us, who alone is worthy of it! Yes, and whoever reaches this degree has come to full maturity.

t: The Many Branches of Our Bond with the Quran, and the Degrees of Holding the Book with Strength
c: Branches of the Relationship with the Quran
x: By branching out your bond with the Noble Quran, I mean that your relationship with it should take many forms, not just one. It is not right to settle for recitation alone, or for memorization alone, or for tafsir and understanding alone. These are all paths, and you must take up each one and walk it, but step by step. We will see how this path unfolds, and what the evidence for it is. In an earlier clip I spoke about branching out our bond with the Noble Quran, and I promised to say more about it later. By branching out your bond with the Noble Quran, I mean that your relationship with it should take many forms, not just one. It is not right to settle for recitation alone, or for memorization alone, or for tafsir and understanding alone. These are all paths, and you must take up each one and walk it, but step by step. We will see how this path unfolds, and what the evidence for it is. The bond with the Noble Quran begins with recitation, as much of it as Allah opens up for you, even if it is just one verse, or two, or three a day. Then you build up gradually: half a juz', then a whole juz', then three, then five. Then, as Allah the Exalted opens the way for you beyond recitation, it is best to move on to memorization, and then to understanding the Quran: reading tafsir and drawing on its books and sciences. And at every one of these stages, you must live by the Noble Quran from the very first letter of it you read. Where did we take this from? From the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in Surat al-Baqarah: (Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise). Fakhr al-Din al-Razi said that the point is to begin in this order: first with recitation (who will recite to them Your verses), and then (and teach them the Book), that is, explain to them the meanings of the Noble Quran; by "the Book" is meant the Quran, and by "wisdom," the Sunnah. (Who will recite to them Your verses): he begins with recitation, and after it come tafsir and understanding (and teach them the Book and wisdom). And so one branch of our bond with the Noble Quran is our bond with the Prophetic Sunnah, which can never be separated from the Noble Quran. That is why you must read the Prophetic Sunnah and come to understand it and know it well; this too is part of your bond with the Noble Quran. Your bond with the Noble Quran is not with the Quran alone, for the Quran is inseparable from the Prophetic Sunnah; and that is why He said: (and teach them the Book and wisdom). Allah the Exalted also says: (So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification [to you]); so one begins with reading, in this order: recitation and memorization, devoting oneself to them; then explanation and tafsir; then contemplation. Allah the Exalted rebuked the People of the Book, saying: (And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming). That is, the bond these People of the Book had with it (meaning here the Jews) was one of reading and nothing more: they pronounced its words correctly, but neither lived by it nor understood its meanings. And why did they not understand its meanings? Because they never devoted themselves to its tafsir and to grasping what it meant, never asked the people of knowledge and learned from them; and so they neither understood it nor lived by it. Why do the People of the Book not live by it? Because they are ignorant of its meanings and its tafsir. Had they studied the tafsir and the meanings and understood them, they could have lived by them, and gained from them, and profited; but they stopped at reciting the words. That is why Ibn Uthaymeen (may Allah have mercy on him) said: In this verse Allah the Exalted rebukes those who read the Book as mere words without understanding its meanings, and it shows how important it is to understand the Noble Quran and its tafsir. Allah the Exalted also says: (Every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein). This parable, the "water parable," as some exegetes called it, is one Allah the Exalted struck about the Noble Quran: the lightning stands for the light of the Noble Quran and its proofs. Every time this lightning, the Quran, flashes, the hypocrites are able to make use of it, walking only as far as its light reaches. So they do gain something from the Noble Quran, but only a little, through the faith they put on display: with it they deceive the believers outwardly, while in truth they deceive only themselves. They walk as far as the Quran lights the way for them, and life stirs in them again, and they benefit; but when that light goes out as they drift away from the Noble Quran, (but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]): they come to a halt, unable to move, unable to benefit. And here is a reflection that came to me on this verse: a person's deeds are measured by his understanding of the Noble Quran. The more his understanding grows, the wider his reading in tafsir, the richer the meanings and knowledge he gains through studying it, the wider his practice of the Noble Quran becomes, and the better his way of life, down to his very thoughts and leanings. And the narrower his understanding of the Noble Quran, the slighter his reading in tafsir, the narrower and scantier his deeds, and the narrower his understanding even of life itself. For to understand the Noble Quran is to understand life. The more you understand the Noble Quran, the better you understand yourself, your life, the people around you, the Hereafter, and so on. Another branch of our bond with the Noble Quran is contemplation. But is contemplation possible without understanding? No, understanding is essential. And so: the wider it grows (every time it lights the way for them), the wider your understanding of the Quran and its meanings, not only do your deeds increase, but Allah the Exalted also opens the doors of contemplation for you. So whenever you find someone to whom contemplation has been opened, know that he reads, studies, and listens to the tafsir of the Noble Quran a great deal. Now I come to holding the Book with strength. When Allah the Exalted raised the mountain, at-Tur, above the Children of Israel to strike awe into them, He took a covenant from them, and part of it was: (Take what We have given you with determination), bi-quwwah : what We have given you of the Torah, of the Book, take it in earnest, with zeal, with energy, and with a firm resolve to preserve it. And this resolve, this strength, is for what? For the branches of this bond: understanding, memorization, and recitation. Take it with resolve, energy, and zeal, not with listlessness and sloth. When I memorized the Noble Quran, all praise be to Allah, I thought, I truly believed, that once I had it by heart I had reached the end and was done. But I discovered that memorizing the Quran is half the strength, not the whole of it. It matters enormously, but it is only part of the strength, not all of it. Then I came to know the strength that comes from studying tafsir, reading it, and reading and listening to it a great deal, and that this is perhaps what completes the second half of the strength. I might even say, to drive the point home: half the strength is memorization, and the other half is understanding. That is why, when someone asked a scholar: What should I do after memorizing the Noble Quran? Should I devote myself to the qira'at or to tafsir? He told him: Devote yourself to tafsir; it comes before the qira'at . This will differ for each person, according to their goals; but this is what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, commanded: that we not busy ourselves with words alone. That is why He rebuked the People of the Book for being taken up with words. The qira'at are beautiful and good, but let a person read, even a little, from the concise, accessible books of tafsir so that he understands; and once he understands, he can set off for the ten qira'at and the other sciences of the Noble Quran. So half the strength is memorization, and the other half is understanding. And when a person is granted the strength of understanding, he is granted, by Allah the Exalted's leave, contemplation and deeds: contemplation and deeds are the fruit of these two strengths. And when contemplation and deeds have been opened up to someone, know that contemplation was opened to him only because he acted. Indeed, I would set them in this order: deeds first, then contemplation; for how could contemplation be opened to someone who does not live by what is in the Book? But living by it begins from the very first letter of the Quran you read. Every time understanding is opened to you, you act on it, and you go on living by the Book all the time. There is no day, no hour, in which we do not live by the Book; no holiday, no break from living by the Quran. Holidays are for worldly work. As for the Quran, it fills every breath and every particle of a person's life, and he lives that life by the Noble Quran. 🎬 Watch the video on YouTube

t: Inner Strength Is a Gift from Allah
x: Every kind of inner strength — patience in all its forms, steadfastness amid trials, courage when you are few, joy and gladness when calamities descend! — all of it is a gift from Allah the Exalted, His support for His servant, and none of it springs from the servant himself Every kind of inner strength — patience in all its forms, steadfastness amid trials, courage when you are few, joy and gladness when calamities descend! — all of it is a gift from Allah the Exalted, His support for His servant, and none of it springs from the servant himself Have you not heard His words: (It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers)? And His words: (And be patient, [O Muhammad], and your patience is not but through Allah) This support descends upon the believer's soul when it is filled with the spirit of the Quran. " Ta'yīd (support) is strengthening, and enabling for the work of the soul. It is derived from al-ayd , which is strength; the Exalted said: ﴿and remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength﴾ [Sad: 17]. And al-ayd is derived from al-yad (the hand), since the hand is the instrument of power; the better view is that it is derived from al-yad , meaning He made him one possessed of a hand, that is, of strength. What is meant here is an inner strength: the strength of the message, and the strength to bear patiently the harm of his people." — Ibn Ashur Patience in carrying the message of the Quran — acting on it, drawing nourishment from it, pondering it and understanding it — comes from Allah's support and His granting of success, not from the servant himself. And patience in carrying the message is what yields patience of the other kinds: patience through calamity, and patience in holding back from sin. Both are the fruit of patience in obedience, and the greatest and nearest of all acts of obedience is the Quran.
